title.zh: 卷八十 志第五十六 食貨四
title.raw: 卷八十 志第五十六 食貨四 Volume 80 Treatises 56: Finance and Economics 4

sentences.zh: 鹽法茶法

translations.literal: Salt Law and Tea Law
translations.idiomatic: Salt Law and Tea Law

sentences.zh: 煮海之利，歷代皆官領之。

translations.literal: The profit from boiling the sea, in every dynasty was led by the government.
translations.idiomatic: The revenue from sea-salt production had been a government monopoly in every dynasty.

sentences.zh: 太祖初起，即立鹽法，置局設官，令商人販鬻，二十取一，以資軍餉。

translations.literal: When the Taizu first rose, he immediately established salt law, set up bureaus and appointed officials, ordered merchants to sell, taking one from twenty, to fund military provisions.
translations.idiomatic: As soon as the founding emperor rose to power, he established a salt monopoly, set up offices and officials, and allowed merchants to retail salt on the condition that one part in twenty was levied to fund the army.

sentences.zh: 既而倍徵之，用胡深言，復初制。

translations.literal: Soon after the levy was doubled; following Hu Shen's advice, the original system was restored.
translations.idiomatic: The rate was soon doubled, but on the advice of Hu Shen the original levy was restored.

sentences.zh: 丙午歲，始置兩淮鹽官。

translations.literal: In the bingwu year, the Lianghuai salt officials were first established.
translations.idiomatic: In the bingwu year, salt officials for the Two Huai regions were first appointed.

sentences.zh: 吳元年置兩浙。

translations.literal: In the first year of Wu, the Two Zhe regions were established.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of the Wu reign, the Two Zhe salt administration was set up.

sentences.zh: 洪武初，諸產鹽地次第設官。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Hongwu, in all salt-producing places officials were set up in succession.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Hongwu reign, officials were appointed one after another at every salt-producing district.

sentences.zh: 都轉運鹽使司六：曰兩淮，曰兩浙，曰長蘆，曰山東，曰福建，曰河東。

translations.literal: Chief salt transport commissioner offices, six: called Lianghuai, Liangzhe, Changlu, Shandong, Fujian, Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: There were six chief salt transport commissioner offices: Lianghuai, Liangzhe, Changlu, Shandong, Fujian, and Hedong.

sentences.zh: 鹽課提舉司七：曰廣東，曰海北，曰四川，曰雲南；

translations.literal: Salt revenue intendant offices, seven: called Guangdong, Haibei, Sichuan, Yunnan;
translations.idiomatic: There were seven salt revenue intendant offices: Guangdong, Haibei, Sichuan, and Yunnan;

sentences.zh: 雲南提舉司凡四，曰黑鹽井，白鹽井，安寧鹽井，五井。

translations.literal: Yunnan intendant offices in all four, called Heiyan Well, Baiyan Well, Anning Salt Well, Wujing.
translations.idiomatic: Yunnan had four such offices, for Heiyan Well, Baiyan Well, Anning Salt Well, and Wujing.

sentences.zh: 又陝西靈州鹽課司一。

translations.literal: Also one Shaanxi Lingzhou salt revenue office.
translations.idiomatic: There was also one salt revenue office at Lingzhou in Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 兩淮所轄分司三，曰泰州，曰淮安，曰通州；

translations.literal: Under Lianghuai, branch offices three, called Taizhou, Huai'an, Tongzhou;
translations.idiomatic: Lianghuai had three branch offices, at Taizhou, Huai'an, and Tongzhou;

sentences.zh: 批驗所二，曰儀真，曰淮安；

translations.literal: Inspection stations two, called Yizhen, Huai'an;
translations.idiomatic: two inspection stations, at Yizhen and Huai'an;

sentences.zh: 鹽場三十，各鹽課司一。

translations.literal: Salt fields thirty, each with one salt revenue office.
translations.idiomatic: thirty salt fields, each with its own salt revenue office.

sentences.zh: 洪武時，歲辦大引鹽三十五萬二千餘引。

translations.literal: In Hongwu times, annually produced large-certificate salt 352,000-odd certificates.
translations.idiomatic: Under Hongwu, the annual quota was more than 352,000 large salt certificates.

sentences.zh: 弘治時，改辦小引鹽，倍之。

translations.literal: In Hongzhi times, changed to small-certificate salt, doubled.
translations.idiomatic: Under Hongzhi, the quota was reckoned in small certificates, which doubled the figure.

sentences.zh: 萬歷時同。

translations.literal: In Wanli times the same.
translations.idiomatic: The Wanli reign followed the same practice.

sentences.zh: 鹽行直隸之應天、甯國、太平、揚州、鳳陽，廬州、安慶、池州、淮安九府，滁、和二州，江西、湖廣二布政司，河南之河南、汝寧、南陽三府及陳州。

translations.literal: Salt circulated in Zhili's Yingtian, Ningguo, Taiping, Yangzhou, Fengyang, Luzhou, Anqing, Chizhou, Huai'an nine prefectures, Chuzhou and Hezhou two prefectures, Jiangxi and Huguang two provincial administrations, Henan's Henan, Runing, Nanyang three prefectures and Chenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Its salt was sold in the nine Zhili prefectures of Yingtian, Ningguo, Taiping, Yangzhou, Fengyang, Luzhou, Anqing, Chizhou, and Huai'an, in Chuzhou and Hezhou, throughout Jiangxi and Huguang, and in the Henan prefectures of Henan, Runing, and Nanyang, as well as Chenzhou.

sentences.zh: 正統中，貴州亦食淮鹽。

translations.literal: In the Zhengtong period, Guizhou also consumed Huai salt.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhengtong reign, Guizhou was also supplied with Lianghuai salt.

sentences.zh: 成化十八年，湖廣衡州、永州改行海北鹽。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year of Chenghua, Huguang's Hengzhou and Yongzhou changed to Haibei salt.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year of Chenghua, Hengzhou and Yongzhou in Huguang were switched to Haibei salt.

sentences.zh: 正德二年，江西贛州、南安、吉安改行廣東鹽。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhengde, Jiangxi's Ganzhou, Nan'an, Ji'an changed to Guangdong salt.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Zhengde, Ganzhou, Nan'an, and Ji'an in Jiangxi were switched to Guangdong salt.

sentences.zh: 所輸邊，甘肅、延綏、寧夏、宣府、大同、遼東、固原、山西神池諸堡。

translations.literal: What was delivered to the border: Gansu, Yansui, Ningxia, Xuanfu, Datong, Liaodong, Guyuan, Shanxi Shenchi and other forts.
translations.idiomatic: Salt was shipped to the frontier at Gansu, Yansui, Ningxia, Xuanfu, Datong, Liaodong, Guyuan, and the Shanxi forts including Shenchi.

sentences.zh: 上供光祿寺、神宮監、內官監。

translations.literal: Supplied upward to the Court of Imperial Entertainments, the Directorate of Palace Ceremonial, and the Directorate of Palace Eunuchs.
translations.idiomatic: It was also supplied to the Court of Imperial Entertainments, the Directorate of Palace Ceremonial, and the Directorate of Palace Eunuchs.

sentences.zh: 歲入太倉餘鹽銀六十萬兩。

translations.literal: Annually entered the Grand Canal storehouse surplus-salt silver 600,000 taels.
translations.idiomatic: Surplus salt revenue remitted to the Taicang treasury came to 600,000 taels a year.

sentences.zh: 兩浙所轄分司四，曰嘉興，曰松江，曰寧、紹，曰溫、台；

translations.literal: Under Liangzhe, branch offices four, called Jiaxing, Songjiang, Ning-Shao, Wen-Tai;
translations.idiomatic: Liangzhe had four branch offices, at Jiaxing, Songjiang, Ningbo-Shaoxing, and Wenzhou-Taizhou;

sentences.zh: 批驗所四，曰杭州，曰紹興，曰嘉興，曰溫州；

translations.literal: Inspection stations four, called Hangzhou, Shaoxing, Jiaxing, Wenzhou;
translations.idiomatic: four inspection stations, at Hangzhou, Shaoxing, Jiaxing, and Wenzhou;

sentences.zh: 鹽場三十五，各鹽課司一。

translations.literal: Salt fields thirty-five, each with one salt revenue office.
translations.idiomatic: thirty-five salt fields, each with its own salt revenue office.

sentences.zh: 洪武時，歲辦大引鹽二十二萬四百餘引。

translations.literal: In Hongwu times, annually produced large-certificate salt 220,400-odd certificates.
translations.idiomatic: Under Hongwu, the annual quota was more than 220,400 large salt certificates.

sentences.zh: 弘治時，改辦小引鹽，倍之。

translations.literal: In Hongzhi times, changed to small-certificate salt, doubled.
translations.idiomatic: Under Hongzhi, the quota was reckoned in small certificates, which doubled the figure.

sentences.zh: 萬歷時同。

translations.literal: In Wanli times the same.
translations.idiomatic: The Wanli reign followed the same practice.

sentences.zh: 鹽行浙江，直隸之松江、蘇州、常州、鎮江、微州五府及廣德州，江西之廣信府。

translations.literal: Salt circulated in Zhejiang, Zhili's Songjiang, Suzhou, Changzhou, Zhenjiang, Huizhou five prefectures and Guangde prefecture, Jiangxi's Guangxin prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Its salt was sold in Zhejiang, in the five Zhili prefectures of Songjiang, Suzhou, Changzhou, Zhenjiang, and Huizhou, in Guangde prefecture, and in Guangxin prefecture in Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 所輸邊，甘肅、延綏、寧夏、固原、山西神池諸堡。

translations.literal: What was delivered to the border: Gansu, Yansui, Ningxia, Guyuan, Shanxi Shenchi and other forts.
translations.idiomatic: Salt was shipped to the frontier at Gansu, Yansui, Ningxia, Guyuan, and the Shanxi forts including Shenchi.

sentences.zh: 歲入太倉餘鹽銀十四萬兩。

translations.literal: Annually entered the Grand Canal storehouse surplus-salt silver 140,000 taels.
translations.idiomatic: Surplus salt revenue remitted to the Taicang treasury came to 140,000 taels a year.

sentences.zh: 明初，置北平河間鹽運司，後改稱河間長蘆。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Ming, established Beiping Hejian Salt Transport Office, later renamed Hejian Changlu.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the dynasty a salt transport office was set up at Hejian in Beiping, later renamed the Hejian-Changlu office.

sentences.zh: 所轄分司二，曰滄州，曰青州；

translations.literal: Under its jurisdiction branch offices two, called Cangzhou, Qingzhou;
translations.idiomatic: It had two branch offices, at Cangzhou and Qingzhou;

sentences.zh: 批驗所二，曰長蘆，曰小直沽；

translations.literal: Inspection stations two, called Changlu, Xiaozhigu;
translations.idiomatic: two inspection stations, at Changlu and Xiaozhigu;

sentences.zh: 鹽場二十四，各鹽課司一。

translations.literal: Salt fields twenty-four, each with one salt revenue office.
translations.idiomatic: twenty-four salt fields, each with its own salt revenue office.

sentences.zh: 洪武時，歲辦大引鹽六萬三幹一百餘引。

translations.literal: In Hongwu times, annually produced large-certificate salt 63,100-odd certificates.
translations.idiomatic: Under Hongwu, the annual quota was more than 63,100 large salt certificates.

sentences.zh: 弘治時，改辦小引鹽十八萬八百餘引。

translations.literal: In Hongzhi times, changed to small-certificate salt 180,800-odd certificates.
translations.idiomatic: Under Hongzhi, the quota was more than 180,800 small salt certificates.

sentences.zh: 萬歷時同。

translations.literal: In Wanli times the same.
translations.idiomatic: The Wanli reign followed the same practice.

sentences.zh: 鹽行北直隸，河南之彰德、衛輝二府。

translations.literal: Salt circulated in North Zhili, Henan's Zhangde and Weihui two prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: Its salt was sold in northern Zhili and in the Henan prefectures of Zhangde and Weihui.

sentences.zh: 所輸邊，宣府、大同、薊州。

translations.literal: What was delivered to the border: Xuanfu, Datong, Jizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Salt was shipped to the frontier at Xuanfu, Datong, and Jizhou.

sentences.zh: 上供郊廟百神祭祀、內府羞膳及給百官有司。

translations.literal: Supplied upward for suburban and temple sacrifices to the hundred spirits, inner palace delicacies, and given to all officials and offices.
translations.idiomatic: It was also supplied for suburban and temple sacrifices, for the palace kitchens, and for the use of officials throughout the government.

sentences.zh: 歲入太倉餘鹽銀十二萬兩。

translations.literal: Annually entered the Grand Canal storehouse surplus-salt silver 120,000 taels.
translations.idiomatic: Surplus salt revenue remitted to the Taicang treasury came to 120,000 taels a year.

sentences.zh: 山東所轄分司二，曰膠萊，曰濱樂；

translations.literal: Under Shandong, branch offices two, called Jiaolai, Binle;
translations.idiomatic: Shandong had two branch offices, at Jiaolai and Binle;

sentences.zh: 批驗所一，曰濼口；

translations.literal: Inspection stations one, called Luokou;
translations.idiomatic: one inspection station, at Luokou;

sentences.zh: 鹽場十九，各鹽課司一。

translations.literal: Salt fields nineteen, each with one salt revenue office.
translations.idiomatic: nineteen salt fields, each with its own salt revenue office.

sentences.zh: 洪武時，歲辦大引鹽十四萬三千三百餘引。

translations.literal: In Hongwu times, annually produced large-certificate salt 143,300-odd certificates.
translations.idiomatic: Under Hongwu, the annual quota was more than 143,300 large salt certificates.

sentences.zh: 弘治時，改辦小引鹽，倍之。

translations.literal: In Hongzhi times, changed to small-certificate salt, doubled.
translations.idiomatic: Under Hongzhi, the quota was reckoned in small certificates, which doubled the figure.

sentences.zh: 萬歷時，九萬六千一百餘引。

translations.literal: In Wanli times, 96,100-odd certificates.
translations.idiomatic: Under Wanli the quota was more than 96,100 certificates.

sentences.zh: 鹽行山東，直隸徐、邳、宿三州，河南開封府，後開封改食河東鹽。

translations.literal: Salt circulated in Shandong, Zhili's Xu, Pi, Su three prefectures, Henan's Kaifeng prefecture; later Kaifeng changed to consume Hedong salt.
translations.idiomatic: Its salt was sold in Shandong, in the Zhili prefectures of Xu, Pi, and Su, and in Kaifeng prefecture in Henan, though Kaifeng was later switched to Hedong salt.

sentences.zh: 所輸邊，遼東及山西神池諸堡。

translations.literal: What was delivered to the border: Liaodong and Shanxi Shenchi and other forts.
translations.idiomatic: Salt was shipped to Liaodong and to the Shanxi forts including Shenchi.

sentences.zh: 歲入太倉餘鹽銀五萬兩。

translations.literal: Annually entered the Grand Canal storehouse surplus-salt silver 50,000 taels.
translations.idiomatic: Surplus salt revenue remitted to the Taicang treasury came to 50,000 taels a year.

sentences.zh: 福建所轄鹽場七，各鹽課司一。

translations.literal: Under Fujian, salt fields seven, each with one salt revenue office.
translations.idiomatic: Fujian had seven salt fields, each with its own salt revenue office.

sentences.zh: 洪武時，歲辦大引鹽十萬四千五百餘引。

translations.literal: In Hongwu times, annually produced large-certificate salt 104,500-odd certificates.
translations.idiomatic: Under Hongwu, the annual quota was more than 104,500 large salt certificates.

sentences.zh: 弘治時，增七百餘引。

translations.literal: In Hongzhi times, increased by 700-odd certificates.
translations.idiomatic: Under Hongzhi the quota rose by more than 700 certificates.

sentences.zh: 萬歷時，減千引。

translations.literal: In Wanli times, reduced by 1,000 certificates.
translations.idiomatic: Under Wanli it was cut by 1,000 certificates.

sentences.zh: 其引曰依山，曰附海。

translations.literal: Its certificates were called yishan, called fuhai.
translations.idiomatic: Its certificates were of two kinds, called "mountain-dependent" and "coast-attached."

sentences.zh: 依山納折色。

translations.literal: Mountain-dependent paid commuted payment.
translations.idiomatic: Mountain-dependent certificates were paid in commuted silver.

sentences.zh: 附海行本色，神宗時亦改折色。

translations.literal: Coast-attached used payment in kind; in Shenzong's time this too was changed to commuted payment.
translations.idiomatic: Coast-attached certificates were delivered in kind until the Shenzong reign, when they too were commuted to silver.

sentences.zh: 鹽行境內。

translations.literal: Salt circulated within the jurisdiction.
translations.idiomatic: Its salt was sold only within the province.

sentences.zh: 歲入太倉銀二萬二千餘兩。

translations.literal: Annually entered the Grand Canal storehouse silver 22,000-odd taels.
translations.idiomatic: Revenue remitted to the Taicang treasury came to more than 22,000 taels a year.

sentences.zh: 河東所轄解鹽，初設東場分司於安邑，成祖時，增設西場於解州，尋復並於東。

translations.literal: Under Hedong, Jie salt; at first the East Field branch office was set at Anyi; in Chengzu's time the West Field was added at Jiezhou, soon merged again into the East.
translations.idiomatic: Hedong administered Jie salt. An eastern field branch was first set up at Anyi; under the Chengzu emperor a western field was added at Jiezhou, but it was soon merged back into the eastern field.

sentences.zh: 正統六年復置西場分司。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Zhengtong the West Field branch office was re-established.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Zhengtong the western field branch was restored.

sentences.zh: 弘治二年增置中場分司。

translations.literal: In the second year of Hongzhi the Central Field branch office was added.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Hongzhi a central field branch was added.

sentences.zh: 洪武時，歲辦小引鹽三十萬四千引。

translations.literal: In Hongwu times, annually produced small-certificate salt 304,000 certificates.
translations.idiomatic: Under Hongwu the annual quota was 304,000 small salt certificates.

sentences.zh: 弘治時，增入萬引。

translations.literal: In Hongzhi times, increased by 10,000 certificates.
translations.idiomatic: Under Hongzhi 10,000 certificates were added to the quota.

sentences.zh: 萬曆中，又增二十萬引。

translations.literal: In the Wanli period, again increased by 200,000 certificates.
translations.idiomatic: During the Wanli reign another 200,000 certificates were added.

sentences.zh: 鹽行陝西之西安、漢中、延安、鳳翔四府，河南之歸德、懷慶、河南、汝寧、南陽五府及汝州，山西之平陽、潞安二府，澤、沁、遼三州。

translations.literal: Salt circulated in Shaanxi's Xi'an, Hanzhong, Yan'an, Fengxiang four prefectures, Henan's Guide, Huaqing, Henan, Runing, Nanyang five prefectures and Ruzhou, Shanxi's Pingyang, Lu'an two prefectures, Ze, Qin, Liao three prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: Its salt was sold in the four Shaanxi prefectures of Xi'an, Hanzhong, Yan'an, and Fengxiang; in the five Henan prefectures of Guide, Huaqing, Henan, Runing, and Nanyang, and in Ruzhou; and in the two Shanxi prefectures of Pingyang and Lu'an, together with Ze, Qin, and Liao prefectures.

sentences.zh: 地有兩見者，鹽得兼行。

translations.literal: Where a place appeared in two lists, salt could circulate in both.
translations.idiomatic: Where a district appeared on more than one list, salt from either source could be sold there.

sentences.zh: 隆慶中，延安改食靈州池鹽。

translations.literal: In the Longqing period, Yan'an changed to consume Lingzhou pool salt.
translations.idiomatic: During the Longqing reign Yan'an was switched to salt from the Lingzhou pools.

sentences.zh: 崇禎中，鳳翔、漢中二府亦改食靈州鹽。

translations.literal: In the Chongzhen period, Fengxiang and Hanzhong two prefectures also changed to consume Lingzhou salt.
translations.idiomatic: During the Chongzhen reign Fengxiang and Hanzhong were also switched to Lingzhou salt.

sentences.zh: 歲入太倉銀四千餘兩，給宣府鎮及大同代府祿糧，抵補山西民糧銀，共十九萬兩有奇。

translations.literal: Annually entered the Grand Canal storehouse silver 4,000-odd taels; supplied Xuanfu garrison and Datong Dai princely establishment stipend grain, offsetting Shanxi civilian grain silver, in all 190,000-odd taels.
translations.idiomatic: Only a little more than 4,000 taels a year went to the Taicang treasury; the rest, totaling more than 190,000 taels, funded stipends for the Xuanfu garrison and the princely establishment at Datong and offset civilian grain payments in Shanxi.

sentences.zh: 陝西靈州有大小鹽池，又有漳縣鹽井、西和鹽井。

translations.literal: Shaanxi Lingzhou had large and small salt pools, and also Zhang county salt wells, Xihe salt wells.
translations.idiomatic: Lingzhou in Shaanxi had large and small salt pools, as well as salt wells in Zhang county and Xihe.

sentences.zh: 洪武時，歲辦鹽，西和十三萬一千五百斤有奇，漳縣五十一萬五千六百斤有奇，靈州二百八十六萬七千四百斤有奇。

translations.literal: In Hongwu times, annually produced salt: Xihe 131,500-odd jin, Zhang county 515,600-odd jin, Lingzhou 2,867,400-odd jin.
translations.idiomatic: Under Hongwu the annual output was more than 131,500 jin at Xihe, more than 515,600 jin at Zhang county, and more than 2,867,400 jin at Lingzhou.

sentences.zh: 弘治時同。

translations.literal: In Hongzhi times the same.
translations.idiomatic: The Hongzhi reign kept the same quotas.

sentences.zh: 萬歷時，三處共辦千二百五十三萬七千六百餘斤。

translations.literal: In Wanli times, the three places together produced 12,537,600-odd jin.
translations.idiomatic: Under Wanli the three sites together produced more than 12,537,600 jin.

sentences.zh: 鹽行陝西之鞏昌、臨洮二府及河州。

translations.literal: Salt circulated in Shaanxi's Gongchang, Lintao two prefectures and Hezhou.
translations.idiomatic: Its salt was sold in the Shaanxi prefectures of Gongchang and Lintao and in Hezhou.

sentences.zh: 歲解寧夏、延綏、固原餉銀三萬六千餘兩。

translations.literal: Annually delivered to Ningxia, Yansui, Guyuan provision silver 36,000-odd taels.
translations.idiomatic: Each year more than 36,000 taels in frontier provisions were sent to Ningxia, Yansui, and Guyuan.

sentences.zh: 廣東所轄鹽場十四，海北所轄鹽場十五，各鹽課司一。

translations.literal: Under Guangdong, salt fields fourteen; under Haibei, salt fields fifteen; each with one salt revenue office.
translations.idiomatic: Guangdong had fourteen salt fields and Haibei fifteen, each field with its own salt revenue office.

sentences.zh: 洪武時，歲辦大引鹽，廣東四萬六千八百餘引，海北二萬七千餘引。

translations.literal: In Hongwu times, annually produced large-certificate salt: Guangdong 46,800-odd certificates, Haibei 27,000-odd certificates.
translations.idiomatic: Under Hongwu the annual quotas were more than 46,800 large certificates for Guangdong and more than 27,000 for Haibei.

sentences.zh: 弘治時，廣東如舊，海北萬九千四百餘引。

translations.literal: In Hongzhi times, Guangdong as before, Haibei 19,400-odd certificates.
translations.idiomatic: Under Hongzhi Guangdong remained unchanged, while Haibei was set at more than 19,400 certificates.

sentences.zh: 萬歷時，廣東小引生鹽三萬二百餘引，小引熟鹽三萬四千六百餘引；

translations.literal: In Wanli times, Guangdong small-certificate raw salt 30,200-odd certificates, small-certificate cured salt 34,600-odd certificates;
translations.idiomatic: Under Wanli Guangdong produced more than 30,200 small certificates of raw salt and more than 34,600 of cured salt;

sentences.zh: 海北小引正耗鹽一萬二千四百餘引。

translations.literal: Haibei small-certificate standard and surplus salt 12,400-odd certificates.
translations.idiomatic: Haibei produced more than 12,400 small certificates counting standard and surplus salt together.

sentences.zh: 鹽有生有熟，熟貴生賤。

translations.literal: Salt had raw and cured; cured was costly, raw was cheap.
translations.idiomatic: Salt was classified as raw or cured, with cured salt priced higher than raw.

sentences.zh: 廣東鹽行廣州、肇慶、惠州、韶州、南雄、潮州六府。

translations.literal: Guangdong salt circulated in Guangzhou, Zhaoqing, Huizhou, Shaozhou, Nanxiong, Chaozhou six prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: Guangdong salt was sold in the six prefectures of Guangzhou, Zhaoqing, Huizhou, Shaozhou, Nanxiong, and Chaozhou.

sentences.zh: 海北鹽行廣東之雷州、高州、廉州、瓊州四府，湖廣之桂陽、郴二州，廣西之桂林、柳州、梧州、潯州、慶遠、南寧、平樂、太平、思明、鎮安十府，田、龍、泗城、奉議、利五州。

translations.literal: Haibei salt circulated in Guangdong's Leizhou, Gaozhou, Lianzhou, Qiongzhou four prefectures, Huguang's Guiyang, Chen two prefectures, Guangxi's Guilin, Liuzhou, Wuzhou, Xunzhou, Qingyuan, Nanning, Pingle, Taiping, Siming, Zhen'an ten prefectures, Tian, Long, Sicheng, Fengyi, Li five prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: Haibei salt was sold in the four Guangdong prefectures of Leizhou, Gaozhou, Lianzhou, and Qiongzhou; in Guiyang and Chen prefectures in Huguang; and in ten Guangxi prefectures—Guilin, Liuzhou, Wuzhou, Xunzhou, Qingyuan, Nanning, Pingle, Taiping, Siming, and Zhen'an—together with Tian, Long, Sicheng, Fengyi, and Li prefectures.

sentences.zh: 歲入太倉鹽課銀萬一千餘兩。

translations.literal: Annually entered the Grand Canal storehouse salt-revenue silver 11,000-odd taels.
translations.idiomatic: Salt revenue remitted to the Taicang treasury came to more than 11,000 taels a year.

sentences.zh: 四川鹽井轄鹽課司十七。

translations.literal: Sichuan salt wells had under their jurisdiction seventeen salt revenue offices.
translations.idiomatic: Sichuan's salt wells were administered through seventeen salt revenue offices.

sentences.zh: 洪武時，歲辦鹽一千一十二萬七千餘斤。

translations.literal: In Hongwu times, annually produced salt 10,127,000-odd jin.
translations.idiomatic: Under Hongwu the annual output was more than 10,127,000 jin.

sentences.zh: 弘治時，辦二千一十七萬六千餘斤。

translations.literal: In Hongzhi times, produced 20,176,000-odd jin.
translations.idiomatic: Under Hongzhi the quota rose to more than 20,176,000 jin.

sentences.zh: 萬曆中，九百八十六萬一千餘斤。

translations.literal: In the Wanli period, 9,861,000-odd jin.
translations.idiomatic: During the Wanli reign output was more than 9,861,000 jin.

sentences.zh: 鹽行四川之成都、敘州、順慶、保寧、夔州五府，潼川、嘉定、廣安、雅、廣元五州縣。

translations.literal: Salt circulated in Sichuan's Chengdu, Xuzhou, Shunqing, Baoning, Kuizhou five prefectures, Tongchuan, Jiading, Guang'an, Ya, Guangyuan five prefectures and counties.
translations.idiomatic: Its salt was sold in the five Sichuan prefectures of Chengdu, Xuzhou, Shunqing, Baoning, and Kuizhou, and in Tongchuan, Jiading, Guang'an, Ya, and Guangyuan.

sentences.zh: 歲解陝西鎮鹽課銀七萬一千餘兩。

translations.literal: Annually delivered to Shaanxi garrison salt-revenue silver 71,000-odd taels.
translations.idiomatic: Each year more than 71,000 taels in salt revenue were sent to the Shaanxi frontier garrison.

sentences.zh: 雲南黑鹽井轄鹽課司三，白鹽井、安寧鹽井各轄鹽課司一，五井轄鹽課司七。

translations.literal: Yunnan Heiyan Well had under jurisdiction three salt revenue offices; Baiyan Well and Anning Salt Well each one; Wujing seven.
translations.idiomatic: Heiyan Well in Yunnan had three salt revenue offices; Baiyan Well and Anning Salt Well each had one; and Wujing had seven.

sentences.zh: 洪武時，歲辦大引鹽萬七千八百餘引。

translations.literal: In Hongwu times, annually produced large-certificate salt 17,800-odd certificates.
translations.idiomatic: Under Hongwu the annual quota was more than 17,800 large salt certificates.

sentences.zh: 弘治時，各井多寡不一。

translations.literal: In Hongzhi times, each well's amount varied.
translations.idiomatic: Under Hongzhi the quotas differed from well to well.

sentences.zh: 萬歷時與洪武同。

translations.literal: In Wanli times the same as Hongwu.
translations.idiomatic: Under Wanli the totals matched those of Hongwu.

sentences.zh: 鹽行境內。

translations.literal: Salt circulated within the jurisdiction.
translations.idiomatic: Its salt was sold only within the province.

sentences.zh: 歲入太倉鹽課銀三萬五千餘兩。

translations.literal: Annually entered the Grand Canal storehouse salt-revenue silver 35,000-odd taels.
translations.idiomatic: Salt revenue remitted to the Taicang treasury came to more than 35,000 taels a year.

sentences.zh: 成祖時，嘗設交阯提舉司，其後交阯失，乃罷。

translations.literal: In Chengzu's time, once established Jiaozhi intendant office; afterward Jiaozhi was lost, then abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Chengzu emperor an intendant office was once set up in Jiaozhi, but it was abolished after the province was lost.

sentences.zh: 遼東鹽場不設官，軍餘煎辦，召商易粟以給軍。

translations.literal: Liaodong salt fields did not set up officials; military dependents boiled salt, summoned merchants to exchange grain to supply the army.
translations.idiomatic: Liaodong salt fields had no government offices; military dependents produced the salt, and merchants were summoned to trade grain for it to supply the troops.

sentences.zh: 凡大引四百斤，小引二百斤。

translations.literal: In general large certificates 400 jin, small certificates 200 jin.
translations.idiomatic: A large certificate was for 400 jin and a small certificate for 200 jin.

sentences.zh: 鹽所產不同：解州之鹽風水所結，寧夏之鹽刮地得之，淮、浙之鹽熬波，川、滇之鹽汲井，閩、粵之鹽積鹵，淮南之鹽煎，淮北之鹽曬，山東之鹽有煎有曬，此其大較也。

translations.literal: Salt produced differed: Jiezhou salt formed by wind and water, Ningxia salt obtained by scraping the ground, Huai and Zhe salt boiled from waves, Chuan and Dian salt drawn from wells, Min and Yue salt accumulated brine, Huainan salt boiled, Huaibei salt sun-dried, Shandong salt both boiled and sun-dried—this was the general comparison.
translations.idiomatic: Salt was produced in different ways: Jiezhou salt formed naturally from wind and water; Ningxia salt was scraped from the ground; Huai and Zhe salt was boiled from seawater; Sichuan and Yunnan salt was drawn from wells; Fujian and Guangdong salt came from accumulated brine; Huainan salt was boiled and Huaibei salt sun-dried; Shandong had both boiling and sun-drying—in broad outline, these were the methods.

sentences.zh: 有明鹽法，莫善於開中。

translations.literal: Among Ming salt law, nothing was better than kaizhong.
translations.idiomatic: Of all Ming salt policies, none worked better than the kaizhong system.

sentences.zh: 洪武三年，山西行省言：「大同糧儲，自陵縣運至太和嶺，路遠費煩。

translations.literal: In the third year of Hongwu, Shanxi provincial administration said: "Datong grain stores, from Ling county transported to Taihe Ridge, the road distant and costs troublesome.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Hongwu the Shanxi provincial administration reported: "Grain for Datong is hauled from Ling county to Taihe Ridge, a long haul that is costly and burdensome.

sentences.zh: 請令商人於大同倉入米一石，太原倉入米一石三斗，給淮鹽一小引。

translations.literal: Request to order merchants at Datong granary to deliver one shi of rice, at Taiyuan granary one shi three dou, and give one small Huai salt certificate.
translations.idiomatic: We ask that merchants who deliver one shi of rice to the Datong granary, or one shi and three dou to the Taiyuan granary, be granted one small Lianghuai salt certificate.

sentences.zh: 商人鬻畢，即以原給引目赴所在官司繳之。

translations.literal: When merchants finished selling, they would take the originally issued certificate to the local office to surrender it.
translations.idiomatic: After selling the salt, the merchant would return the original certificate to the local office.

sentences.zh: 如此則轉運費省而邊儲充。」

translations.literal: Thus transport costs would be saved and border stores filled.
translations.idiomatic: In this way transport costs would be saved and frontier granaries filled.

sentences.zh: 帝從之。

translations.literal: The emperor followed it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved the proposal.

sentences.zh: 召商輸糧而與之鹽，謂之開中。

translations.literal: Summoning merchants to deliver grain and giving them salt was called kaizhong.
translations.idiomatic: Summoning merchants to deliver grain in exchange for salt was called kaizhong.

sentences.zh: 其後各行省邊境，多召商中鹽以為軍儲。

translations.literal: Afterward in each province's border regions, merchants were often summoned to tender for salt as military stores.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter frontier provinces widely used merchant tenders for salt to build up military grain reserves.

sentences.zh: 鹽法邊計，相輔而行。

translations.literal: Salt law and border planning proceeded in mutual support.
translations.idiomatic: Salt policy and frontier finance thus worked hand in hand.

sentences.zh: 四年定中鹽例，輸米臨濠、開封、陳橋、襄陽、安陸、荊州、歸州、大同、太原、孟津、北平、河南府、陳州、北通州諸倉，計道里近遠，自五石至一石有差。

translations.literal: In the fourth year fixed salt-tender regulations: delivering rice to Linhao, Kaifeng, Chenqiao, Xiangyang, Anlu, Jingzhou, Guizhou, Datong, Taiyuan, Mengjin, Beiping, Henan prefecture, Chenzhou, North Tongzhou and other granaries, calculating distance near and far, from five shi to one shi with differences.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year the salt-tender quotas were fixed for granaries at Linhao, Kaifeng, Chenqiao, Xiangyang, Anlu, Jingzhou, Guizhou, Datong, Taiyuan, Mengjin, Beiping, Henan prefecture, Chenzhou, and North Tongzhou, with required deliveries ranging from five shi to one shi according to distance.

sentences.zh: 先後增減，則例不一，率視時緩急，米直高下，中納者利否。

translations.literal: Increases and decreases followed one another, so regulations were not uniform, generally depending on urgency of the times, grain price high or low, whether tenderers profited or not.
translations.idiomatic: Rates were adjusted repeatedly, so the rules were never uniform and generally followed the urgency of the moment, grain prices, and whether tendering was profitable.

sentences.zh: 道遠地險，則減而輕之。

translations.literal: Where the road was distant and terrain dangerous, it was reduced and lightened.
translations.idiomatic: Where routes were long and terrain difficult, the required delivery was reduced.

sentences.zh: 編置勘合及底簿，發各布政司及都司、衛所。

translations.literal: Compiled verification tallies and master registers, issued to each provincial administration and regional command, guard posts.
translations.idiomatic: Verification tallies and master registers were compiled and issued to provincial administrations, regional commands, and guard posts.

sentences.zh: 商納糧畢，書所納糧及應支鹽數，齎赴各轉運提舉司照數支鹽。

translations.literal: When merchants finished delivering grain, they wrote the grain delivered and salt to be disbursed, carried to each transport or intendant office to receive salt according to the number.
translations.idiomatic: After delivering grain, the merchant recorded the amount delivered and the salt due, then presented the document at the transport or intendant office to receive the allotted salt.

sentences.zh: 轉運諸司亦有底簿比照，勘合相符，則如數給與。

translations.literal: Transport offices also had master registers for comparison; when verification tallies matched, they gave according to the number.
translations.idiomatic: The transport offices checked their master registers, and when the tally matched, salt was issued in full.

sentences.zh: 鬻鹽有定所，刊諸銅版，犯私鹽者罪至死，偽造引者如之，鹽與引離，即以私鹽論。

translations.literal: Selling salt had fixed places, engraved on bronze plates; violators of private salt were punished up to death, forging certificates likewise; when salt and certificate separated, it was treated as private salt.
translations.idiomatic: Salt could be sold only at designated places, as engraved on bronze plates; private salt dealing was punishable by death, as was forging certificates, and salt sold without its certificate was treated as contraband.

sentences.zh: 仁宗立，以鈔法不通，議所以斂之之道。

translations.literal: When Renzong ascended, because paper money did not circulate, they discussed ways to gather it in.
translations.idiomatic: When the Renzong emperor came to the throne, paper money had ceased to circulate, and officials debated how to recall it.

sentences.zh: 戶部尚書夏原吉請令有鈔之家中鹽，遂定各鹽司中鹽則例，滄州引三百貫，河東、山東半之，福建、廣東百貫。

translations.literal: Minister of Revenue Xia Yuanji requested ordering those with paper money to tender for salt, then fixed each salt office's tender regulations: Cangzhou certificate 300 guan, Hedong and Shandong half, Fujian and Guangdong 100 guan.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Revenue Xia Yuanji proposed letting holders of paper notes tender for salt, and fixed the rates at 300 guan per certificate at Cangzhou, half that at Hedong and Shandong, and 100 guan at Fujian and Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 宣德元年停中鈔例。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xuande the paper-note tender regulation was stopped.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Xuande the paper-note tender was abolished.

sentences.zh: 三年，原吉以北京官吏、軍、匠糧餉不支，條上預備策，言：「中鹽舊則太重，商賈少至，請更定之。」

translations.literal: In the third year, Yuanji because Beijing officials, troops, and artisans' provisions were insufficient, submitted preparatory measures, saying: "The old salt-tender regulation was too heavy, merchants rarely came; request to revise it.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year Yuanji reported that provisions for Beijing officials, troops, and artisans were running short and proposed emergency measures: "The old salt-tender rates are too high and merchants seldom come; we ask that they be revised.

sentences.zh: 乃定每引自二斗五升至一斗五升有差，召商納米北京。

translations.literal: Then fixed each certificate from two dou five sheng to one dou five sheng with differences, summoning merchants to deliver rice to Beijing.
translations.idiomatic: The rate was then set between two dou five sheng and one dou five sheng per certificate, and merchants were summoned to deliver rice to Beijing.

sentences.zh: 戶部尚書郭敦言：「中鹽則例已減，而商來者少，請以十分為率，六分支與納米京倉者，四分支與遼東、永平、山海、甘肅、大同、宣府、萬全已納米者。

translations.literal: Minister of Revenue Guo Dun said: "Salt-tender regulations have been reduced, yet merchants coming are few; request taking ten parts as the rate, six parts given to those delivering rice to Beijing granaries, four parts to Liaodong, Yongping, Shanhai, Gansu, Datong, Xuanfu, Wansai who already delivered rice.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Revenue Guo Dun said: "Although tender rates have been cut, few merchants are coming. We propose dividing salt ten ways: six parts for those delivering rice to Beijing granaries and four for those who have already delivered rice at Liaodong, Yongping, Shanhai, Gansu, Datong, Xuanfu, and Wansai.

sentences.zh: 他處中納悉停之。」

translations.literal: Tendering elsewhere was all stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Tendering at all other locations should be suspended.

sentences.zh: 又言：「洪武中，中鹽客商年久物故，代支者多虛冒，請按引給鈔十錠。」

translations.literal: Also said: "In Hongwu times, salt-tender merchants after many years died; substitutes disbursing were mostly false; request according to certificates to give ten ingots of paper money.
translations.idiomatic: He also said: "Under Hongwu, many merchants who tendered for salt have died over the years, and many substitute claims are fraudulent. We ask that ten ingots of paper money be paid per outstanding certificate."

sentences.zh: 帝皆從之，而命倍給其鈔。

translations.literal: The emperor all followed, and ordered double payment of their paper money.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved all these proposals and ordered double payment in paper money.

sentences.zh: 甘肅、寧夏、大同、宣府、獨石、永平道險遠，趨中者少，許寓居官員及軍餘有糧之家納米豆中鹽。

translations.literal: Gansu, Ningxia, Datong, Xuanfu, Dushi, Yongping—roads dangerous and distant, few rushed to tender; permitted resident officials and military dependents with grain households to deliver rice and beans to tender for salt.
translations.idiomatic: Because Gansu, Ningxia, Datong, Xuanfu, Dushi, and Yongping were remote and hazardous, few merchants tendered there, so resident officials and military dependents with grain were allowed to deliver rice and beans in exchange for salt.

sentences.zh: 正統三年，寧夏總兵官史昭以邊軍缺馬，而延慶、平涼官吏軍民多養馬，乃奏請納馬中鹽。

translations.literal: In the third year of Zhengtong, Ningxia commander-in-chief Shi Zhao because frontier troops lacked horses, while Yanqing and Pingliang officials, troops, and civilians raised many horses, memorialized requesting horse delivery for salt tender.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Zhengtong, Ningxia commander Shi Zhao reported that frontier troops lacked horses while many were raised by officials, soldiers, and civilians in Yanqing and Pingliang, and asked that horses be accepted in exchange for salt.

sentences.zh: 上馬一匹與鹽百引，次馬八十引。

translations.literal: Top-grade horse one gave salt 100 certificates, second-grade horse 80 certificates.
translations.idiomatic: A top-grade horse earned 100 salt certificates and a second-grade horse 80.

sentences.zh: 既而定邊諸衛遞增二十引。

translations.literal: Soon after, Dingbian and other guards successively added 20 certificates.
translations.idiomatic: Guards in the Dingbian area soon received an additional 20 certificates per horse.

sentences.zh: 其後河州中納者，上馬二十五引，中減五引；

translations.literal: Afterward for Hezhou tenders, top-grade horse 25 certificates, second-grade reduced five certificates;
translations.idiomatic: Later at Hezhou a top-grade horse earned 25 certificates and a second-grade horse five fewer;

sentences.zh: 松潘中納者，上馬三十五引，中減五引。

translations.literal: For Songpan tenders, top-grade horse 35 certificates, second-grade reduced five certificates.
translations.idiomatic: at Songpan a top-grade horse earned 35 certificates and a second-grade horse five fewer.

sentences.zh: 久之，復如初制。

translations.literal: After a long time, restored to the original system.
translations.idiomatic: In time the original rates were restored.

sentences.zh: 中馬之始，驗馬乃掣鹽，既而納銀於官以市馬，銀入布政司，宗祿、屯糧、修邊、振濟輾轉支銷，銀盡而馬不至，而邊儲亦自此告匱矣。

translations.literal: At the beginning of horse tendering, horses were inspected then salt issued; soon after silver was delivered to government to buy horses; silver entered the provincial administration, princely stipends, garrison grain, border repair, relief successively disbursed; silver exhausted but horses did not arrive, and border stores from this also reported depletion.
translations.idiomatic: At first horses were inspected before salt was issued, but soon silver was paid to the government to buy horses instead. The silver passed through the provincial treasury and was spent on princely stipends, garrison grain, border repairs, and relief until it was gone, yet the horses never came—and frontier reserves were exhausted as well.

sentences.zh: 於是召商中淮、浙、長廬鹽以納之，令甘肅中鹽者，淮鹽十七，浙鹽十三。

translations.literal: Thereupon merchants were summoned to tender Huai, Zhe, and Changlu salt to deliver it; ordered Gansu salt tenders: Huai salt seventeen parts, Zhe salt thirteen parts.
translations.idiomatic: Merchants were then summoned to tender Lianghuai, Liangzhe, and Changlu salt for delivery to Gansu, in a ratio of seventeen parts Huai salt to thirteen parts Zhe salt.

sentences.zh: 淮鹽惟納米麥，浙鹽兼收豌豆、青稞。

translations.literal: Huai salt only accepted rice and wheat; Zhe salt also accepted peas and highland barley.
translations.idiomatic: Huai tenders accepted only rice and wheat, while Zhe tenders also accepted peas and highland barley.

sentences.zh: 因淮鹽直貴，商多趨之，故令淮、浙兼中也。

translations.literal: Because Huai salt's value was costly, merchants mostly rushed to it; therefore ordered Huai and Zhe combined tendering.
translations.idiomatic: Because Huai salt was more valuable, merchants preferred it, so Huai and Zhe tenders were combined.

sentences.zh: 明初仍宋、元舊制，所以優恤灶戶者甚厚，給草場以供樵採，堪耕者許開墾，仍免其雜役，又給工本米，引一石。

translations.literal: Early Ming followed Song and Yuan old systems; favors to salt-makers were very generous: gave pasture for fuel gathering, where arable permitted opening land, still exempted miscellaneous corvée, also gave production-cost rice, one shi per certificate.
translations.idiomatic: Early Ming followed Song and Yuan practice and treated salt-makers generously: they were given pasture for fuel, allowed to reclaim arable land, exempted from miscellaneous corvée, and granted one shi of production-cost rice per certificate.

sentences.zh: 置倉於場，歲撥附近州縣倉儲及兌軍餘米以待給，兼支錢鈔，以米價為準。

translations.literal: Set up granaries at the fields; annually allocated nearby prefecture and county stores and transport troops' surplus rice for disbursement, also paid money and paper notes according to rice price.
translations.idiomatic: Granaries were set up at the salt fields, supplied each year from nearby county stores and surplus transport grain, with cash and paper notes paid according to the price of rice.

sentences.zh: 尋定鈔數，淮、浙引二貫五百文，河間、廣東、海北、山東、福建、四川引二貫。

translations.literal: Soon fixed paper-note amounts: Huai and Zhe certificates 2 guan 500 wen; Hejian, Guangdong, Haibei, Shandong, Fujian, Sichuan certificates 2 guan.
translations.idiomatic: Cash payments were then fixed at 2 guan 500 wen per certificate for Huai and Zhe and 2 guan for Hejian, Guangdong, Haibei, Shandong, Fujian, and Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 灶戶雜犯死罪以上止予杖，計日煎鹽以贖。

translations.literal: Salt-makers for miscellaneous offenses above death penalty received only beating, counting days boiling salt to redeem.
translations.idiomatic: Salt-makers guilty of capital crimes short of murder were punished only with beating and allowed to redeem the sentence by boiling salt for a set number of days.

sentences.zh: 後設總催，多朘削灶戶。

translations.literal: Later general collectors were set up, mostly squeezing salt-makers.
translations.idiomatic: Later general collectors were appointed, and they often squeezed the salt-makers.

sentences.zh: 至正統時，灶戶貧困，逋逃者多，松江所負課六十餘萬。

translations.literal: By Zhengtong times, salt-makers were impoverished, many fled arrears, Songjiang office owed revenue 600,000-odd.
translations.idiomatic: By the Zhengtong reign salt-makers were impoverished, many fled, and the Songjiang office alone was more than 600,000 units in arrears.

sentences.zh: 民訴於朝，命直隸巡撫周忱兼理鹽課。

translations.literal: The people appealed at court; ordered Zhili grand coordinator Zhou Chen concurrently to manage salt revenue.
translations.idiomatic: The people petitioned the throne, and Grand Coordinator Zhou Chen of Zhili was ordered to take charge of salt revenue as well.

sentences.zh: 忱條上鑄鐵釜、恤鹵丁、選總催、嚴私販四事，且請於每年正課外，帶徵逋課。

translations.literal: Chen submitted four items: casting iron kettles, caring for brine workers, selecting general collectors, strictly banning private sale; and requested beyond annual regular revenue to collect arrears additionally.
translations.idiomatic: Chen proposed four measures—casting iron kettles, relief for brine workers, careful selection of collectors, and strict suppression of private trade—and asked that arrears be collected in addition to the annual quota.

sentences.zh: 帝從其請。

translations.literal: The emperor followed his request.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved his request.

sentences.zh: 命分逋課為六，以六載畢徵。

translations.literal: Ordered dividing arrears into six parts, to be fully collected in six years.
translations.idiomatic: Arrears were to be divided into six installments and collected over six years.

sentences.zh: 當是時，商人有自永樂中候支鹽，祖孫相代不得者。

translations.literal: At this time, merchants had since Yongle waited for salt disbursement, generations passing without receiving it.
translations.idiomatic: At this time some merchants had been waiting for salt since the Yongle reign, with generations passing without ever receiving it.

sentences.zh: 乃議仿洪武中例，而加鈔錠以償之，願守支者聽。

translations.literal: Then discussed following Hongwu precedent, adding paper ingots to compensate them; those wishing to wait for disbursement were permitted.
translations.idiomatic: It was proposed to follow the Hongwu precedent of paying compensation in paper money, while those who preferred to keep waiting for salt could do so.

sentences.zh: 又以商人守支年久，雖減輕開中，少有上納者，議他鹽司如舊制，而淮、浙、長蘆以十分為率，八分給守支商，曰常股，二分收貯於官，曰存積，遇邊警，始召商中納。

translations.literal: Also because merchants waiting for disbursement many years, though kaizhong was lightened, few delivered; discussed other salt offices as old system, but Huai, Zhe, Changlu taking ten parts as rate, eight parts given to waiting merchants called changgu, two parts stored by government called cunji, when border alarm, then summoned merchants to tender.
translations.idiomatic: Because merchants had waited so long that even reduced kaizhong rates drew few deliveries, other salt offices kept the old system, but for Huai, Zhe, and Changlu salt was divided ten ways: eight parts went to waiting merchants as the regular allotment, and two parts were held by the government as reserve stock to be tendered only when the frontier was threatened.

sentences.zh: 常股、存積之名由此始。

translations.literal: The names changgu and cunji began from this.
translations.idiomatic: The terms changgu and cunji date from this reform.

sentences.zh: 凡中常股者價輕，中存積者價重，然人甚苦守支，爭趨存積，而常股壅矣。

translations.literal: All who tendered changgu had light price, cunji had heavy price; yet people greatly suffered waiting, rushed to cunji, and changgu was blocked.
translations.idiomatic: Tendering for the regular allotment was cheap and for reserve stock expensive, but merchants hated the long wait and rushed to reserve stock, leaving the regular allotment unsold.

sentences.zh: 景帝時，邊圉多故，存積增至六分。

translations.literal: In Jingdi's time, the border had many troubles; cunji increased to six parts.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Jingdi emperor, with frequent frontier emergencies, the reserve share was raised to six tenths.

sentences.zh: 中納邊糧，兼納穀草、秋青草，秋青草三當穀草二。

translations.literal: Tendering border grain, also accepted grain fodder and autumn green fodder; three parts autumn green fodder equaled two parts grain fodder.
translations.idiomatic: Frontier tenders accepted grain, hay, and autumn grazing fodder, with three parts of autumn fodder counting as two of hay.

sentences.zh: 廣東之鹽，例不出境，商人率市守關吏，越市廣西。

translations.literal: Guangdong salt, by regulation did not leave the border; merchants mostly bribed border guards, crossed to sell in Guangxi.
translations.idiomatic: Guangdong salt was not supposed to leave the province, but merchants usually bribed border guards and smuggled it into Guangxi.

sentences.zh: 巡撫葉盛以為任之則廢法，禁之則病商，請令入米餉邊，乃許出境，公私交利焉。

translations.literal: Grand coordinator Ye Sheng thought allowing it would void the law, forbidding would harm merchants; requested ordering grain delivery to supply the border, then permit leaving the border—public and private both profited.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Coordinator Ye Sheng argued that tolerating the trade would void the law but banning it would ruin merchants, and proposed allowing export if merchants delivered grain to the frontier—a compromise that benefited both state and trade.

sentences.zh: 成化初，歲洊災，京儲不足，召商於淮、徐、德州水次倉中鹽。

translations.literal: Early Chenghua, years repeatedly disaster, capital stores insufficient, summoned merchants at Huai, Xu, Dezhou riverside granaries to tender for salt.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Chenghua, after repeated crop failures left the capital short of grain, merchants were summoned to tender for salt at riverside granaries in Huai, Xu, and Dezhou.

sentences.zh: 舊例中鹽，戶部出榜召商，無徑奏者。

translations.literal: Old regulation for salt tender, the Ministry of Revenue posted notices summoning merchants; none petitioned directly.
translations.idiomatic: Under the old rules, the Ministry of Revenue posted public notices to summon merchants for salt tenders; no one was to petition directly.

sentences.zh: 富人呂銘等託勢要奏中兩淮存積鹽，中旨允之。

translations.literal: Rich men Lü Ming and others relied on powerful patrons to memorialize tendering for Lianghuai reserve salt; imperial rescript approved.
translations.idiomatic: Wealthy men such as Lü Ming used powerful patrons to petition for Lianghuai reserve salt, and an imperial rescript approved.

sentences.zh: 戶部尚書馬昂不能執正，鹽法之壞自此始。

translations.literal: Minister of Revenue Ma Ang could not uphold correctness; the ruin of salt law began from this.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Revenue Ma Ang failed to uphold the rules, and the breakdown of salt policy began here.

sentences.zh: 勢豪多攙中，商人既失利，江南、北軍民因造遮洋大船，列械販鹽。

translations.literal: Powerful families mostly muscled into tenders; merchants already lost profit; Jiangnan and north military and civilians therefore built ocean-going large ships, arrayed weapons to sell salt.
translations.idiomatic: Powerful families crowded into tenders, merchants lost money, and troops and civilians in north and south built armed ocean-going ships to smuggle salt.

sentences.zh: 乃為重法，私販、窩隱俱論死，家屬徙邊衛，夾帶越境者充軍。

translations.literal: Then made severe law: private sale and harboring both punished by death, families exiled to border guards, carrying across borders punished by military service.
translations.idiomatic: Harsh penalties followed: private dealing and harboring were capital crimes, families were exiled to frontier guards, and smuggling across borders was punished by military service.

sentences.zh: 然不能遏止也。

translations.literal: Yet could not stop it.
translations.idiomatic: Yet smuggling could not be stopped.

sentences.zh: 十九年頗減存積之數，常股七分，而存積三分。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year considerably reduced reserve amount: changgu seven parts, cunji three parts.
translations.idiomatic: In the nineteenth year the reserve share was cut so that the regular allotment was seven tenths and reserve stock three.

sentences.zh: 然商人樂有見鹽，報中存積者爭至，遂仍增至六分。

translations.literal: Yet merchants delighted in visible salt; those reporting cunji tenders rushed in, so it was again increased to six parts.
translations.idiomatic: Merchants preferred salt they could receive at once, however, and rushed to tender for reserve stock, so the reserve share was raised again to six tenths.

sentences.zh: 淮、浙鹽猶不能給，乃配支長廬、山東以給之。

translations.literal: Huai and Zhe salt still could not supply; then allocated Changlu and Shandong to supply them.
translations.idiomatic: Even Huai and Zhe salt could not meet demand, so Changlu and Shandong salt was allotted to make up the shortfall.

sentences.zh: 一人兼支數處，道遠不及親赴，邊商輒貿引於近地富人。

translations.literal: One person received from several places; roads distant could not go in person; border merchants then traded certificates to nearby rich men.
translations.idiomatic: When one merchant held certificates from several regions and could not travel to each in person, frontier merchants sold their certificates to local wealthy men.

sentences.zh: 自是有邊商、內商之分。

translations.literal: From this there were border merchants and interior merchants.
translations.idiomatic: From this arose the distinction between frontier merchants and interior merchants.

sentences.zh: 內商之鹽不能速獲，邊商之引又不賤售，報中寢怠，存積之滯遂與常股等。

translations.literal: Interior merchants' salt could not be quickly obtained; border merchants' certificates were not cheaply sold; tender reports grew slack; cunji backlog became equal to changgu.
translations.idiomatic: Interior merchants could not get salt quickly, frontier merchants would not sell certificates cheaply, tenders dwindled, and reserve stock piled up like the regular allotment.

sentences.zh: 憲宗末年，閹宦竊勢，奏討淮、浙鹽無算，兩淮積欠至五百餘萬引，商引壅滯。

translations.literal: Late in Xianzong's reign, eunuchs stole power, memorialized requesting Huai and Zhe salt without limit; Lianghuai accumulated arrears to 5,000,000-odd certificates; merchant certificates blocked.
translations.idiomatic: Late in the Xianzong reign eunuchs seized power and obtained limitless grants of Huai and Zhe salt; Lianghuai fell more than five million certificates in arrears and merchant certificates piled up unsold.

sentences.zh: 至孝宗時，而買補餘鹽之議興矣。

translations.literal: By Xiaozong's time, the proposal to buy and supplement surplus salt arose.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Xiaozong emperor the policy of purchasing surplus salt to supplement official quotas was introduced.

sentences.zh: 餘鹽者，灶戶正課外所餘之鹽也。

translations.literal: Surplus salt was what salt-makers had beyond regular revenue.
translations.idiomatic: Surplus salt was whatever salt-makers produced beyond their official quota.

sentences.zh: 洪武初制，商支鹽有定場，毋許越場買補；

translations.literal: Hongwu initial regulation: merchants receiving salt had fixed fields, not permitted to cross fields to buy supplement;
translations.idiomatic: Under the early Hongwu rules, merchants received salt only at designated fields and were forbidden to buy supplements elsewhere;

sentences.zh: 勤灶有餘鹽送場司，二百斤為一引，給米一石。

translations.literal: diligent salt-makers with surplus salt sent to field office, 200 jin as one certificate, given one shi of rice.
translations.idiomatic: diligent salt-makers who had surplus salt delivered it to the field office, 200 jin counting as one certificate, and received one shi of rice.

sentences.zh: 其鹽召商開中，不拘資次給與。

translations.literal: That salt summoned merchants for kaizhong, not bound by seniority in giving.
translations.idiomatic: That salt was opened to merchant tenders without regard to priority.

sentences.zh: 成化後，令商收買，而勸借米麥以振貧灶。

translations.literal: After Chenghua, ordered merchants to purchase, and urged lending rice and wheat to relieve poor salt-makers.
translations.idiomatic: After Chenghua merchants were required to buy it, and were urged to lend rice and wheat to relieve impoverished salt-makers.

sentences.zh: 至是清理兩淮鹽法，侍郎李嗣請令商人買餘鹽補官引，而免其勸借，且停各邊開中，俟逋課完日，官為賣鹽，三分價直，二充邊儲，而留其一以補商人未交鹽價。

translations.literal: At this time clearing Lianghuai salt law, Vice Minister Li Si requested ordering merchants to buy surplus salt to supplement official certificates, exempting urged lending, and stopping frontier kaizhong everywhere; when arrears were finished, government would sell salt, three parts of price value, two for border stores, one retained to supplement merchants' unpaid salt price.
translations.idiomatic: When Lianghuai salt policy was reformed, Vice Minister Li Si proposed that merchants buy surplus salt to fill official certificates, ending forced loans to salt-makers and suspending frontier kaizhong until arrears were cleared. The government would then sell salt, applying three parts of the proceeds: two for frontier stores and one to cover merchants' unpaid salt prices.

sentences.zh: 由是以餘鹽補充正課，而鹽法一小變。

translations.literal: From this surplus salt supplemented regular revenue, and salt law had a small change.
translations.idiomatic: Surplus salt thus supplemented the regular quota, marking a minor shift in salt policy.

sentences.zh: 明初，各邊開中商人，招民墾種，築臺堡自相保聚，邊方菽粟無甚貴之時。

translations.literal: Early Ming, frontier kaizhong merchants recruited people to reclaim and plant, built platform forts to protect one another; frontier grain and beans had no very costly times.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the dynasty frontier merchants who tendered for salt recruited settlers, built fortified farms, and kept grain cheap on the border.

sentences.zh: 成化間，始有折納銀者，然未嘗著為令也。

translations.literal: In Chenghua period, there began commuted payment in silver, yet it was never written as regulation.
translations.idiomatic: During Chenghua silver payments began to appear, but they were never formally codified.

sentences.zh: 弘治五年，商人困守支，戶部尚書葉淇請召商納銀運司，類解太倉，分給各邊。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Hongzhi, merchants distressed by waiting, Minister of Revenue Ye Qi requested summoning merchants to deliver silver to transport offices, classified and sent to Taicang, distributed to each border.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Hongzhi, with merchants exhausted by long waits, Minister of Revenue Ye Qi proposed that they pay silver to transport offices, which would remit it to Taicang for distribution to the frontiers.

sentences.zh: 每引輸銀三四錢有差，視國初中米直加倍，而商無守支之苦，一時太倉銀累至百餘萬。

translations.literal: Each certificate delivered silver three or four qian with differences; compared to founding rice price doubled, yet merchants had no waiting distress; for a time Taicang silver accumulated to more than a million.
translations.idiomatic: Merchants paid three or four qian of silver per certificate—roughly double the early grain equivalent—and were freed from waiting, while Taicang silver reserves briefly exceeded one million taels.

sentences.zh: 然赴邊開中之法廢，商屯撤業，菠粟翔貴，邊儲日虛矣。

translations.literal: Yet the method of going to the border for kaizhong was abolished; merchant colonies withdrew business; grain and beans soared costly; border stores daily grew empty.
translations.idiomatic: Yet frontier kaizhong was abandoned, merchant colonies were abandoned, grain prices soared, and frontier reserves dwindled daily.

sentences.zh: 武宗之初，以鹽法日壞，令大臣王瓊、張憲等分道清理，而慶雲侯周壽、壽甯侯張鶴各令家人奏買長蘆、兩淮鹽引。

translations.literal: Early in Wuzong, because salt law daily worsened, ordered grand ministers Wang Qiong, Zhang Xian and others to clear by separate routes; Marquis of Qingyun Zhou Shou and Marquis of Shouning Zhang He each had household members memorialize to buy Changlu and Lianghuai salt certificates.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Wuzong reign, as salt policy deteriorated, ministers Wang Qiong and Zhang Xian were sent to investigate by separate routes, while the Marquis of Qingyun Zhou Shou and the Marquis of Shouning Zhang He had their retainers petition to buy Changlu and Lianghuai salt certificates.

sentences.zh: 戶部尚書韓文執不可，中旨許之。

translations.literal: Minister of Revenue Han Wen upheld that it could not be done; imperial rescript permitted it.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Revenue Han Wen objected, but an imperial rescript approved the purchases.

sentences.zh: 織造太監崔杲又奏乞長蘆鹽一萬二千引，戶部以半予之。

translations.literal: Weaving supervisor eunuch Cui Gao again memorialized begging 12,000 Changlu salt certificates; the Ministry of Revenue gave half.
translations.idiomatic: Weaving supervisor eunuch Cui Gao also petitioned for 12,000 Changlu certificates, and the ministry granted half.

sentences.zh: 帝欲全予，大學士劉健等力爭，李東陽語尤切。

translations.literal: The emperor wished to give all; Grand Secretaries Liu Jian and others strongly contested; Li Dongyang's words especially sharp.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wanted to grant the full amount, but Grand Secretaries Liu Jian and others protested vigorously, Li Dongyang most sharply of all.

sentences.zh: 帝不悅。

translations.literal: The emperor was displeased.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was displeased.

sentences.zh: 健等復疏爭，乃從部議。

translations.literal: Jian and others again memorialized contesting; then followed the ministry's proposal.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Jian and the others protested again in memorials, and the emperor accepted the ministry's proposal.

sentences.zh: 權要開中既多，又許買餘鹽，一引有用至十餘年者。

translations.literal: Powerful figures' kaizhong already many, also permitted buying surplus salt; one certificate sometimes used for more than ten years.
translations.idiomatic: With powerful families dominating tenders and surplus salt sales allowed, a single certificate could remain in use for more than ten years.

sentences.zh: 正德二年始申截舊引角之令，立限追繳，而每引增納紙價及振濟米麥。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhengde began enforcing the order to cut off old certificate corners, set limits for recovery, and each certificate added paper price and relief rice and wheat.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Zhengde old certificates were ordered cut and recovered within a deadline, with added fees for paper costs and relief grain per certificate.

sentences.zh: 引價重而課壅如故矣。

translations.literal: Certificate price heavy yet revenue blockage as before.
translations.idiomatic: Certificate fees rose, yet revenue remained blocked as before.

sentences.zh: 先是成化初，都御史韓雍於肇慶、梧州、清遠、南雄立抽鹽廠，官鹽一引，抽銀五分，許帶餘鹽四引，引抽銀一錢。

translations.literal: Earlier, early Chenghua, Censor-in-Chief Han Yong at Zhaoqing, Wuzhou, Qingyuan, Nanxiong established salt levy stations; official salt one certificate, levied silver five fen, permitted carrying four surplus certificates, each certificate levied one qian.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, early in Chenghua, Censor-in-Chief Han Yong set up salt levy stations at Zhaoqing, Wuzhou, Qingyuan, and Nanxiong: five fen of silver per official certificate and one qian per surplus certificate, with up to four surplus certificates allowed.

sentences.zh: 都御史秦紘許增帶餘鹽六引，抽銀六錢。

translations.literal: Censor-in-Chief Qin Hong permitted increasing carried surplus salt to six certificates, levying six qian.
translations.idiomatic: Censor-in-Chief Qin Hong allowed six surplus certificates and a levy of six qian.

sentences.zh: 及是增至九錢，而不復抽官引。

translations.literal: At this time increased to nine qian, and no longer levied official certificates.
translations.idiomatic: The levy was now raised to nine qian, but official certificates were no longer taxed.

sentences.zh: 引目積滯，私鹽通行，乃用戶部郎中丁致祥請，復紘舊法。

translations.literal: Certificates accumulated stagnant, private salt circulated; then used Ministry of Revenue Director Ding Zhixiang's request, restored Hong's old method.
translations.idiomatic: Certificates piled up and private salt flourished, so on the proposal of Ministry Director Ding Zhixiang, Hong's old method was restored.

sentences.zh: 而他處商人夾帶餘鹽，掣割納價，惟多至三百斤者始罪之。

translations.literal: Elsewhere merchants carried surplus salt, cut and paid price; only when exceeding 300 jin was it punished.
translations.idiomatic: Elsewhere merchants who carried surplus salt paid a cut fee, and only loads exceeding 300 jin were punished.

sentences.zh: 淮、浙、長蘆引鹽，常股四分，以給各邊主兵及工役振濟之需；

translations.literal: Huai, Zhe, Changlu certificate salt: changgu four parts, to supply each frontier's standing troops and corvée relief needs;
translations.idiomatic: For Huai, Zhe, and Changlu certificate salt, four tenths were the regular allotment, set aside to meet frontier garrison pay and relief for corvée labor.

sentences.zh: 存積六分，非國家大事，邊境有警，未嘗妄開。

translations.literal: Cunji six parts; unless great state affair or frontier alarm, never rashly opened.
translations.idiomatic: Six tenths were reserve stock, which was never opened without cause except for major state affairs or frontier alarms.

sentences.zh: 開必邊臣奏討，經部覆允，未有商人擅請及專請淮鹽者。

translations.literal: Opening required frontier officials to memorialize and request, ministry reply approval; never had merchants privately request or exclusively request Huai salt.
translations.idiomatic: Opening reserve stock required a frontier official's petition and ministry approval; merchants were never allowed to request tenders on their own or to demand Huai salt exclusively.

sentences.zh: 弘治間，存積鹽甚多。

translations.literal: During Hongzhi, cunji salt very much.
translations.idiomatic: During the Hongzhi reign, reserve stock salt accumulated in great quantities.

sentences.zh: 正德時，權幸遂奏開殘鹽，改存積、常股皆為正課，且皆折銀。

translations.literal: During Zhengde, powerful favorites then memorialized opening remnant salt, changed cunji and changgu all into regular quota, and all converted to silver.
translations.idiomatic: Under Zhengde, court favorites memorialized to open remnant salt, reclassified both reserve stock and the regular allotment as standard quota, and converted all payments to silver.

sentences.zh: 邊臣緩急無備，而勢要佔中賣窩，價增數倍。

translations.literal: Frontier officials in emergency had no preparation, while powerful figures monopolized tenders and sold franchises, prices increased several fold.
translations.idiomatic: Frontier officials had no reserves for emergencies, while the powerful monopolized tenders and sold franchise rights at several times the normal price.

sentences.zh: 商人引納銀八錢，無所獲利，多不願中，課日耗絀。

translations.literal: Merchants per certificate paid eight qian silver, gained nothing; many unwilling to tender; revenue daily dwindled.
translations.idiomatic: Merchants paying eight qian per certificate made no profit, so many refused to tender, and revenue dwindled day by day.

sentences.zh: 奸黠者夾帶影射，弊端百出。

translations.literal: Crafty wicked ones smuggled by concealment and shadow schemes; abuses emerged in every direction.
translations.idiomatic: Crafty men smuggled salt by concealment and fraudulent reporting, and abuses multiplied on every side.

sentences.zh: 鹽臣承中璫風旨，復列零鹽、所鹽諸目以假之。

translations.literal: Salt officials following palace eunuchs' instructions, again listed remnant salt, office salt and other categories as pretexts.
translations.idiomatic: Salt officials, acting on instructions from palace eunuchs, again invented categories such as remnant salt and office salt as pretexts for abuse.

sentences.zh: 世宗登極詔，首命裁革。

translations.literal: The Jiajing accession edict first ordered cutting and abolishing them.
translations.idiomatic: The Jiajing Emperor's accession edict ordered these practices abolished as its first reform.

sentences.zh: 未幾，商人逯俊等夤緣近幸，以增價為名，奏買殘餘等鹽。

translations.literal: Before long, merchants Lu Jun and others curried favor with court intimates, under the name of raising prices memorialized to buy remnant and surplus salt.
translations.idiomatic: Before long, merchants such as Lu Jun curried favor with the Emperor's intimates and, under the pretext of raising prices, memorialized to purchase remnant and surplus salt.

sentences.zh: 戶部尚書秦金執不允，帝特令中兩淮額鹽三十萬引於宣府。

translations.literal: Minister of Revenue Qin Jin held firm in refusal; Emperor specially ordered tendering three hundred thousand Lianghuai quota certificates at Xuanfu.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Revenue Qin Jin refused to approve, but the Emperor specially ordered three hundred thousand Lianghuai quota certificates tendered at Xuanfu.

sentences.zh: 金言：「奸人佔中淮鹽，賣窩罔利，使山東、長蘆等鹽別無搭配，積之無用。

translations.literal: Jin said: "Wicked men monopolize Huai salt tenders, sell franchises for profit, causing Shandong, Changlu and other salt to have no matching allotment, accumulating uselessly.
translations.idiomatic: Qin Jin said, "Wicked men monopolize Huai salt tenders and sell franchise rights for profit, leaving Shandong and Changlu salt with no matching allotment and piling up unused.

sentences.zh: 虧國用，誤邊儲，莫此為甚。」

translations.literal: Harming state revenue, misleading frontier stores—nothing worse than this."
translations.idiomatic: It drains state revenue and undermines frontier stores—nothing could be more damaging.

sentences.zh: 御史高世魁亦爭之。

translations.literal: Censor Gao Shikui also argued against it.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Gao Shikui also argued against the plan.

sentences.zh: 詔減淮引十萬，分兩浙、長蘆鹽給之。

translations.literal: Edict reduced Huai certificates one hundred thousand, divided Liangzhe and Changlu salt to supply it.
translations.idiomatic: An edict cut the Huai allocation by one hundred thousand certificates and made up the difference with Liangzhe and Changlu salt.

sentences.zh: 金復言：「宣、大俱重鎮，不宜令奸商自擇便利，但中宣府。」

translations.literal: Jin again said: "Xuan and Datong both major garrisons; not suitable to let wicked merchants choose convenience themselves; only tender at Xuanfu."
translations.idiomatic: Qin Jin again said, "Xuanfu and Datong are both major garrisons. Wicked merchants should not be allowed to choose whichever post suits them; tenders should go to Xuanfu alone.

sentences.zh: 帝可之。

translations.literal: The Emperor approved it.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 已而俊等請以十六人中宣府，十一人中大同，竟從其請。

translations.literal: Before long Jun and others requested using one hundred sixty thousand to tender at Xuanfu, one hundred ten thousand at Datong; in the end their request was granted.
translations.idiomatic: Before long, Lu Jun and his associates asked for one hundred sixty thousand certificates at Xuanfu and one hundred ten thousand at Datong, and in the end their request was granted.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖五年從給事中管律奏，乃復常股存積四六分之制。

translations.literal: Jiajing fifth year, following Supervising Secretary Guan Lu's memorial, then restored changgu-cunji four-six parts system.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Jiajing, on the memorial of Supervising Secretary Guan Lu, the four-six split between the regular allotment and reserve stock was restored.

sentences.zh: 然是時餘鹽盛行，正鹽守支日久，願中者少；

translations.literal: Yet at this time surplus salt flourished; official salt waiting for disbursement long, those willing to tender few;
translations.idiomatic: Yet by then surplus salt had become widespread: official salt required long waits for disbursement, and few merchants were willing to tender for it;

sentences.zh: 餘鹽第領勘合，即時支賣，願中者多。

translations.literal: Surplus salt only needed obtaining tally, immediately disbursed and sold; those willing to tender many.
translations.idiomatic: surplus salt required only a tally for immediate disbursement and sale, and many merchants were eager to tender for it.

sentences.zh: 自弘治時以餘鹽補正課，初以償逋課，後令商人納價輸部濟邊。

translations.literal: Since Hongzhi times used surplus salt to supplement official quota; initially to repay arrears, later ordered merchants pay price and deliver to ministry to aid frontier.
translations.idiomatic: Since Hongzhi, surplus salt had supplemented the official quota—first to repay arrears, and later by requiring merchants to pay a fee remitted to the ministry to support the frontier.

sentences.zh: 至嘉靖時，延綏用兵，遼左缺餉，盡發兩淮餘鹽七萬九千餘引於二邊開中。

translations.literal: By Jiajing times, Yansui used troops, Liaodong left lacked pay; fully issued Lianghuai surplus salt seventy-nine thousand-odd certificates on both frontiers for kaizhong.
translations.idiomatic: By the Jiajing reign, campaigns in Yansui and pay shortages in Liaodong led the court to release all seventy-nine thousand-odd Lianghuai surplus certificates for kaizhong on both frontiers.

sentences.zh: 自是餘鹽行。

translations.literal: From this surplus salt circulated.
translations.idiomatic: From that point surplus salt became standard practice.

sentences.zh: 其始尚無定額，未幾，兩淮增引一百四十餘萬，每引增餘鹽二百六十五斤。

translations.literal: At first still without fixed quota; before long Lianghuai added certificates one million four hundred thousand-odd, each certificate added surplus salt two hundred sixty-five jin.
translations.idiomatic: At first there was still no fixed quota, but before long Lianghuai added more than 1.4 million certificates, with an extra 265 jin of surplus salt per certificate.

sentences.zh: 引價，淮南納銀一兩九錢，淮北一兩五錢，又設處置、科罰名色，以苛斂商財。

translations.literal: Certificate price: south of Huai paid silver one liang nine qian, north of Huai one liang five qian; also established disposal and penalty categories to harshly extract merchant wealth.
translations.idiomatic: Certificate fees were set at 1.9 liang of silver south of the Huai and 1.5 liang north of it, while new categories of administrative penalties and fines were imposed to squeeze merchants ever harder.

sentences.zh: 於是正鹽未派，先估餘鹽，商灶俱困。

translations.literal: Thus before official salt was allocated, surplus salt was estimated first; merchants and salt-makers both distressed.
translations.idiomatic: Official salt had not yet been allocated when surplus salt was assessed first, leaving both merchants and salt-makers in distress.

sentences.zh: 奸黠者藉口官買餘鹽，夾販私煎。

translations.literal: Crafty wicked ones used official purchase of surplus salt as pretext, smuggling private boiling.
translations.idiomatic: Crafty men used the official purchase of surplus salt as a cover to smuggle privately boiled salt.

sentences.zh: 法禁無所施，鹽法大壞。

translations.literal: Law and prohibition had nowhere to apply; salt law greatly ruined.
translations.idiomatic: The law could no longer be enforced, and the salt system collapsed.

sentences.zh: 十三年，給事中管懷理言：「鹽法之壞，其弊有六。

translations.literal: Thirteenth year, Supervising Secretary Guan Huaili said: "Salt law's ruin—its abuses have six.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year, Supervising Secretary Guan Huaili said, "The salt system has broken down, and the abuses are six in number.

sentences.zh: 開中不時，米價騰貴，召糴之難也。

translations.literal: Kaizhong not timely, rice prices soaring—the difficulty of summoning grain purchases.
translations.idiomatic: Kaizhong was opened irregularly while grain prices soared, making it hard to summon grain deliveries.

sentences.zh: 勢豪大家，專擅利權，報中之難也。

translations.literal: Powerful great families monopolized profit rights—the difficulty of tendering.
translations.idiomatic: Powerful great families monopolized the profits, making it hard to report successful tenders.

sentences.zh: 官司科罰，吏胥侵索，輸納之難也。

translations.literal: Official offices imposed penalties, clerks extorted—the difficulty of delivering payments.
translations.idiomatic: Official penalties and clerk extortion made payment difficult.

sentences.zh: 下場挨掣，動以數年，守支之難也。

translations.literal: At salt yard waiting for weighing, often several years—the difficulty of waiting for disbursement.
translations.idiomatic: Waiting at the salt yard for weighing often took years, making disbursement unbearably slow.

sentences.zh: 定價太昂，息不償本，取贏之難也。

translations.literal: Fixed price too high, profit not recovering capital—the difficulty of making gain.
translations.idiomatic: Fixed prices were too high for profit to cover costs, so merchants could scarcely earn anything.

sentences.zh: 私鹽四出，官鹽不行，市易之難也。

translations.literal: Private salt went out everywhere, official salt did not circulate—the difficulty of market exchange.
translations.idiomatic: Private salt flooded the market while official salt would not move, making trade impossible.

sentences.zh: 有此六難，正課壅矣，而司計者因設餘鹽以佐之。

translations.literal: Having these six difficulties, official quota blocked; revenue officials therefore established surplus salt to assist it.
translations.idiomatic: Because of these six difficulties the official quota was blocked, so revenue officials introduced surplus salt to shore it up.

sentences.zh: 餘鹽利厚，商固樂從，然不以開邊而以解部，雖歲入距萬，無益軍需。

translations.literal: Surplus salt profit thick, merchants naturally willing to follow; yet not used for frontier kaizhong but remitted to ministry; though yearly income tens of thousands, no benefit to military needs.
translations.idiomatic: Surplus salt was highly profitable and merchants were glad to buy it, yet it was remitted to the ministry rather than used for frontier kaizhong, so even revenues in the tens of thousands did nothing for military supply.

sentences.zh: 嘗考祖宗時，商人中鹽納價甚輕，而灶戶煎鹽工本甚厚，今鹽價十倍於前，而工本不能十一，何以禁私鹽使不行也？

translations.literal: I have examined that in ancestral times, merchants tendering salt paid very light price, yet salt-makers' boiling production cost very generous; now salt price ten times former, yet production cost not even one tenth—how can private salt be forbidden from circulating?
translations.idiomatic: I have looked back to the founding era, when merchants paid very little to tender for salt while salt-makers received generous production subsidies. Today salt prices are ten times what they were, yet production support is less than a tenth of what it was—how can private salt be kept off the market?

sentences.zh: 故欲通鹽法，必先處餘鹽，欲處餘鹽，必多減正價。

translations.literal: Therefore to unblock salt law, must first handle surplus salt; to handle surplus salt, must greatly reduce official price.
translations.idiomatic: To restore the salt system, surplus salt must be dealt with first; and to deal with surplus salt, the official price must be cut sharply.

sentences.zh: 大抵正鹽賤，則私販自息。

translations.literal: Generally when official salt is cheap, private smuggling naturally ceases.
translations.idiomatic: In general, when official salt is cheap, private smuggling dies away on its own.

sentences.zh: 今宜定價，每引正鹽銀五錢，餘鹽二錢五分，不必解赴太倉，俱令開中關支，餘鹽以盡收為度。

translations.literal: Now should fix price: each certificate official salt five qian silver, surplus salt two qian five fen; need not remit to Taicang, all allow kaizhong frontier disbursement; surplus salt take full collection as measure.
translations.idiomatic: Prices should now be fixed at five qian of silver per official certificate and two qian five fen for surplus salt. Neither need be sent to Taicang; both should be disbursed through kaizhong at the frontier, with surplus salt collected in full.

sentences.zh: 正鹽價輕，既利於商；

translations.literal: Official salt price light, already benefiting merchants;
translations.idiomatic: Lower official salt prices would benefit merchants;

sentences.zh: 餘鹽收盡，又利於灶。

translations.literal: Surplus salt fully collected, again benefiting salt-makers.
translations.idiomatic: and collecting all surplus salt would benefit the salt-makers as well.

sentences.zh: 未有商灶俱利，而國課不充者也。」

translations.literal: Never has there been merchants and salt-makers both profiting while state revenue not filled."
translations.idiomatic: When merchants and salt-makers both prosper, state revenue has never failed to be met.

sentences.zh: 事下所司，戶部覆，以為餘鹽銀仍解部如故，而邊餉益虛矣。

translations.literal: Matter referred to responsible offices; Ministry of Revenue replied, deeming surplus salt silver still remitted to ministry as before, and frontier pay grew emptier.
translations.idiomatic: The proposal was referred to the responsible offices. The Ministry of Revenue replied that surplus salt silver should still be remitted to the ministry as before, and frontier pay grew ever more depleted.

sentences.zh: 至二十年，帝以變亂鹽法由餘鹽，敕罷之。

translations.literal: By twentieth year, Emperor because surplus salt disturbed salt law, ordered its abolition.
translations.idiomatic: By the twentieth year, the Emperor held surplus salt responsible for wrecking the salt system and ordered it abolished.

sentences.zh: 淮、浙、長蘆悉復舊法，夾帶者割沒入官，應變賣者以時估為準。

translations.literal: Huai, Zhe, Changlu all restored old methods; smugglers confiscated for state; what should be sold evaluated by current market price.
translations.idiomatic: Huai, Zhe, and Changlu all returned to the old rules; smuggled salt was confiscated for the state, and salt slated for sale was priced by current market valuation.

sentences.zh: 御史吳瓊又請各邊中鹽者皆輸本色。

translations.literal: Censor Wu Qiong again requested all frontier kaizhong tenderers deliver goods in kind.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Wu Qiong also requested that all frontier kaizhong tenderers deliver grain and fodder in kind.

sentences.zh: 然令甫下，吏部尚書許訁贊即請復開餘鹽以足邊用。

translations.literal: Yet order just issued, Minister of Personnel Xu Zan immediately requested reopening surplus salt to fill frontier needs.
translations.idiomatic: Hardly had the order been issued when Minister of Personnel Xu Zan asked to reopen surplus salt to meet frontier needs.
