sentences.zh: 戶部覆從之，餘鹽復行矣。

translations.literal: Ministry of Revenue replied in assent; surplus salt circulated again.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of Revenue agreed, and surplus salt was put back into circulation.

sentences.zh: 先是，十六年令兩浙僻邑，官商不行之處，山商每百斤納銀八分，給票行鹽。

translations.literal: Earlier, sixteenth year ordered remote Liangzhe counties where official merchants did not operate: mountain merchants per hundred jin paid eight fen silver, given tickets to sell salt.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, in the sixteenth year, remote counties in Liangzhe where official merchants did not operate were allowed mountain merchants to pay eight fen of silver per hundred jin and receive tickets to sell salt.

sentences.zh: 其後多侵奪正引，官商課缺，引壅二百萬，候掣必五六載。

translations.literal: Afterwards they greatly encroached on official certificates; official merchant revenue lacked; certificates blocked two million; waiting for weighing required five or six years.
translations.idiomatic: Later they encroached heavily on official certificates, official merchant revenue fell short, two million certificates piled up, and waiting for weighing took five or six years.

sentences.zh: 於是有預徵、執抵、季掣之法。

translations.literal: Therefore there were methods of advance collection, offset holding, and seasonal weighing.
translations.idiomatic: Rules were therefore introduced for advance collection, offset holding, and seasonal weighing.

sentences.zh: 預徵者，先期輸課，不得私為去留。

translations.literal: Advance collection: pay revenue ahead of schedule, may not privately decide stay or leave.
translations.idiomatic: Advance collection meant paying revenue ahead of schedule, with no private discretion over timing.

sentences.zh: 執抵者，執現在運鹽水程，復持一引以抵一引。

translations.literal: Offset holding: hold current salt transport waterway permit, also hold one certificate to offset one certificate.
translations.idiomatic: Offset holding meant presenting the current salt transport permit and using one certificate to offset another.

sentences.zh: 季掣，則以納課先後為序，春不得遲於夏，夏不得超於春也。

translations.literal: Seasonal weighing: order by sequence of revenue payment; spring may not delay past summer, summer may not jump ahead of spring.
translations.idiomatic: Seasonal weighing set the order by time of payment: spring could not be delayed into summer, nor summer advanced ahead of spring.

sentences.zh: 然票商納稅即掣賣，預徵諸法徒厲引商而已。

translations.literal: Yet ticket merchants paying tax immediately weighed and sold; advance collection methods only harmed certificate merchants.
translations.idiomatic: Ticket merchants, however, paid tax and sold at once, so the advance-collection rules only burdened certificate merchants.

sentences.zh: 靈州鹽池，自史昭中馬之議行，邊餉虧缺，甘肅米直石銀五兩，戶部因奏停中馬，召商納米中鹽。

translations.literal: Lingzhou salt ponds—since Shi Zhao's horse tender proposal was implemented, frontier pay deficient; Gansu rice price per shi five liang silver; Ministry therefore memorialized stopping horse tender, summoning merchants to deliver grain for salt tender.
translations.idiomatic: At the Lingzhou salt ponds, after Shi Zhao's horse-tender proposal took effect frontier pay fell short and Gansu rice reached five liang of silver per shi. The Ministry therefore memorialized to stop horse tenders and summon merchants to deliver grain in exchange for salt certificates.

sentences.zh: 二十七年令開中者止納本色糧草。

translations.literal: Twenty-seventh year ordered kaizhong tenderers only deliver grain and fodder in kind.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-seventh year, kaizhong tenderers were ordered to deliver only grain and fodder in kind.

sentences.zh: 三十二年令河東以六十二萬引為額，合正餘鹽為一，而革餘鹽名。

translations.literal: Thirty-second year ordered Hedong set quota at six hundred twenty thousand certificates, combined official and surplus salt into one, and abolished surplus salt name.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-second year, Hedong was given a quota of 620,000 certificates, official and surplus salt were merged into one category, and the surplus salt designation was abolished.

sentences.zh: 時都御史王紳、御史黃國用議：兩淮灶戶餘鹽，每引官給銀二錢，以充工本，增收三十五萬引，名為工本鹽。

translations.literal: At that time Censor-in-Chief Wang Shen and Censor Huang Guoyong proposed: Lianghuai salt-makers' surplus salt, per certificate government gives two qian silver to cover production cost, additionally collect three hundred fifty thousand certificates, named production-cost salt.
translations.idiomatic: Censor-in-Chief Wang Shen and Censor Huang Guoyong then proposed that for Lianghuai salt-makers' surplus salt the government pay two qian per certificate as production cost, and that 350,000 additional certificates be levied under the name production-cost salt.

sentences.zh: 令商人中額鹽二引，帶中工本鹽一引，抵主兵年例十七萬六千兩有奇。

translations.literal: Ordered merchants tender two quota certificates, carry one production-cost certificate; offset standing army annual quota one hundred seventy-six thousand-odd liang.
translations.idiomatic: Merchants were to tender for two quota certificates and one production-cost certificate together, covering the standing army's annual quota of more than 176,000 liang.

sentences.zh: 從其請。

translations.literal: Their request was granted.
translations.idiomatic: The request was granted.

sentences.zh: 初，淮鹽歲課七十萬五千引，開邊報中為正鹽，後益餘鹽納銀解部。

translations.literal: Initially, Huai salt annual quota seven hundred five thousand certificates; kaizhong frontier reports as official salt; later added surplus salt silver payment remitted to ministry.
translations.idiomatic: Initially Huai salt yielded 705,000 certificates a year, with frontier kaizhong tenders counted as official salt; later surplus salt fees in silver were added and remitted to the ministry.

sentences.zh: 至是通前額凡一百五萬引，額增三之一。

translations.literal: At this point including prior quota altogether one million five hundred thousand certificates; quota increased by one third.
translations.idiomatic: The total quota now reached 1.5 million certificates including earlier allotments, an increase of one third.

sentences.zh: 行之數年，積滯無所售，鹽法壅不行。

translations.literal: After several years of implementation, accumulated stagnation nowhere to sell; salt law blocked and not functioning.
translations.idiomatic: After several years salt piled up unsold and the system ceased to function.

sentences.zh: 言事者屢陳工本為鹽贅疣。

translations.literal: Memorialists repeatedly stated production-cost salt was salt's excrescence.
translations.idiomatic: Memorialists repeatedly argued that production-cost salt was a useless growth on the salt system.

sentences.zh: 戶部以國用方絀，年例無所出，因之不變。

translations.literal: Ministry of Revenue because state revenue just deficient, annual quota nowhere to come from, therefore unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of Revenue, finding state revenue already strained and no other source for the annual quota, left the policy unchanged.

sentences.zh: 江西故行淮鹽三十九萬引，後南安、贛州、吉安改行廣鹽，惟南昌諸府行淮鹽二十七萬引。

translations.literal: Jiangxi originally circulated Huai salt three hundred ninety thousand certificates; later Nan'an, Ganzhou, Ji'an switched to Guang salt; only Nanchang prefectures circulated Huai salt two hundred seventy thousand certificates.
translations.idiomatic: Jiangxi had originally sold 390,000 Huai certificates, but later Nan'an, Ganzhou, and Ji'an switched to Guang salt, leaving only the Nanchang prefectures on 270,000 Huai certificates.

sentences.zh: 既而私販盛行，袁州、臨江、瑞州則私食廣鹽，撫州、建昌私食福鹽。

translations.literal: Before long private smuggling flourished; Yuanzhou, Linjiang, Ruizhou privately consumed Guang salt; Fuzhou, Jianchang privately consumed Fu salt.
translations.idiomatic: Before long private trade flourished: Yuanzhou, Linjiang, and Ruizhou consumed Guang salt illicitly, while Fuzhou and Jianchang consumed Fu salt.

sentences.zh: 於是淮鹽僅行十六萬引。

translations.literal: Thus Huai salt only circulated one hundred sixty thousand certificates.
translations.idiomatic: Huai salt sales in the province fell to only 160,000 certificates.

sentences.zh: 數年之間，國計大絀。

translations.literal: Within several years, state accounts greatly deficient.
translations.idiomatic: Within a few years state revenue suffered a major shortfall.

sentences.zh: 巡撫馬森疏其害，請於峽江縣建橋設關，扼閩、廣要津，盡復淮鹽額，稍增至四十七萬引。

translations.literal: Grand Coordinator Ma Sen memorialized its harm, requested building bridge and customs at Xiajiang county, controlling Fujian-Guangdong key route, fully restoring Huai salt quota, slightly increased to four hundred seventy thousand certificates.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Coordinator Ma Sen memorialized the damage and asked to build a bridge and customs post at Xiajiang county to control the Fujian-Guangdong corridor, fully restore the Huai salt quota, and raise it slightly to 470,000 certificates.

sentences.zh: 未久橋毀，增額二十萬引復除矣。

translations.literal: Before long bridge destroyed; increased quota two hundred thousand certificates again removed.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the bridge was destroyed, and the added quota of 200,000 certificates was withdrawn.

sentences.zh: 三十九年，帝欲整鹽法，乃命副都御史鄢懋卿總理淮、浙、山東、長蘆鹽法。

translations.literal: Thirty-ninth year, Emperor wished to reform salt law, then appointed Vice Censor-in-Chief Yan Maoqing to oversee Huai, Zhe, Shandong, Changlu salt law.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-ninth year, wishing to reform the salt system, the Emperor appointed Vice Censor-in-Chief Yan Maoqing to oversee salt policy in Huai, Zhe, Shandong, and Changlu.

sentences.zh: 懋卿，嚴嵩黨也，苞苴無虛日。

translations.literal: Maoqing was Yan Song faction; gifts never absent a day.
translations.idiomatic: Maoqing was a member of Yan Song's faction and accepted bribes without a day's interruption.

sentences.zh: 兩淮額鹽銀六十一萬有奇，自設工本鹽，增九十萬，懋卿復增之，遂滿百萬。

translations.literal: Lianghuai quota salt silver six hundred ten thousand-odd; since establishing production-cost salt, added nine hundred thousand; Maoqing again increased it, reaching full one million.
translations.idiomatic: Lianghuai quota salt had yielded a little over 610,000 liang of silver; production-cost salt added 900,000, and Maoqing raised it further until the total reached one million.

sentences.zh: 半年一解。

translations.literal: Remitted every half year.
translations.idiomatic: It was remitted to the capital every half year.

sentences.zh: 又蒐括四司殘鹽，共得銀幾二百萬，一時詡為奇功。

translations.literal: Also searched remnant salt from four offices, total silver nearly two million; momentarily praised as remarkable achievement.
translations.idiomatic: He also seized remnant salt from the four salt offices, raising nearly two million liang of silver, which was briefly hailed as a remarkable achievement.

sentences.zh: 乃立克限法，每卒一人，季限獲私鹽有定數；

translations.literal: Then established quota enforcement law: each patrolman per season must seize private salt in fixed amount;
translations.idiomatic: He then imposed quota enforcement: each patrolman had a fixed amount of private salt to seize each season;

sentences.zh: 不及數，輒削其僱役錢。

translations.literal: Falling short, immediately cut their hired service pay.
translations.idiomatic: and if he fell short, his hired-service pay was cut.

sentences.zh: 邏卒經歲有不得支一錢者，乃共為私販，以矣大利，甚至劫估舶，誣以鹽盜而執之，流毒遍海濱矣。

translations.literal: Patrolmen some year not receiving a single qian, then jointly became private smugglers to obtain great profit, even robbing merchant boats, falsely accusing as salt pirates and arresting them; poison spread throughout coastal regions.
translations.idiomatic: Some patrolmen went a full year without receiving a single qian, then turned to smuggling together for great profit, even robbing merchant vessels and falsely arresting them as salt pirates, until the abuse spread along the entire coast.

sentences.zh: 嵩失勢，巡鹽御史徐爌言：「兩淮鹽法，曰常股，曰存積，曰水鄉，共七十萬引有奇。

translations.literal: When Song lost power, salt censor Xu Huang said: "Lianghuai salt law: called changgu, called cunji, called water districts, totaling seven hundred thousand-odd certificates.
translations.idiomatic: After Yan Song fell from power, salt censor Xu Huang said, "The Lianghuai salt system comprised the regular allotment, reserve stock, and water-district categories, totaling a little over 700,000 certificates.

sentences.zh: 引二百斤，納銀八分。

translations.literal: Each certificate two hundred jin, pays eight fen silver.
translations.idiomatic: Each certificate was for 200 jin and required eight fen of silver.

sentences.zh: 永樂以後，引納粟二斗五升，下場關支，四散發賣，商人之利亦什五焉。

translations.literal: After Yongle, certificate paid two dou five sheng grain, disbursed at salt yard, distributed for sale; merchant profit also one part in fifteen.
translations.idiomatic: After Yongle, each certificate required 2.5 dou of grain, salt was disbursed at the yard and sold widely, and merchants still cleared a profit of about fifteen percent.

sentences.zh: 近年，正鹽之外，加以餘鹽；

translations.literal: In recent years, beyond official salt, added surplus salt;
translations.idiomatic: In recent years surplus salt was added on top of official salt;

sentences.zh: 餘鹽之外，又加工本；

translations.literal: Beyond surplus salt, again added production cost;
translations.idiomatic: on top of surplus salt came production-cost salt;

sentences.zh: 工本不足，乃有添單；

translations.literal: Production cost insufficient, then had supplementary tickets;
translations.idiomatic: when production-cost salt was not enough, there were supplementary tickets;

sentences.zh: 添單不足，又加添引。

translations.literal: Supplementary tickets insufficient, again added supplementary certificates.
translations.idiomatic: and when supplementary tickets were not enough, still more certificates were added.

sentences.zh: 懋卿趨利目前，不顧其後，是誤國亂政之尤者。

translations.literal: Maoqing pursued present profit, heedless of consequences—this is the worst sort misleading the state and disordering governance.
translations.idiomatic: Maoqing chased immediate profit without regard for consequences—the worst kind of policy that misleads the state and wrecks governance.

sentences.zh: 方今災荒疊告，鹽場淹沒，若欲取盈百萬，必至逃亡。

translations.literal: Now disasters and famine repeatedly reported, salt fields flooded; if wishing to take full million, must lead to flight.
translations.idiomatic: Disasters and famine are reported one after another and salt fields are flooded; if the goal is still to collect a full million, people will flee.

sentences.zh: 弦急欲絕，不棘於此。」

translations.literal: Bowstring tight about to snap—nothing more urgent than this."
translations.idiomatic: The bowstring is stretched to the breaking point—nothing is more urgent than this.

sentences.zh: 於是悉罷懋卿所增者。

translations.literal: Thereupon all Maoqing's additions were abolished.
translations.idiomatic: All of Maoqing's increases were then abolished.

sentences.zh: 四十四年，巡鹽御史硃炳如奏罷兩淮工本鹽。

translations.literal: Forty-fourth year, salt censor Zhu Bingru memorialized abolishing Lianghuai production-cost salt.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-fourth year, salt censor Zhu Bingru memorialized to abolish Lianghuai production-cost salt.

sentences.zh: 自葉淇變法，邊儲多缺。

translations.literal: Since Ye Qi's reform, frontier stores mostly lacked.
translations.idiomatic: Since Ye Qi's reform, frontier stores had often run short.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖八年以後，稍復開中，邊商中引，內商守支。

translations.literal: After Jiajing eighth year, slightly restored kaizhong; frontier merchants tender certificates, interior merchants wait for disbursement.
translations.idiomatic: After the eighth year of Jiajing, kaizhong was partly restored: frontier merchants tendered for certificates and interior merchants waited to receive salt.

sentences.zh: 末年，工本鹽行，內商有數年不得掣者，於是不樂買引，而邊商困，因營求告掣河鹽。

translations.literal: In final years, production-cost salt circulated; interior merchants some several years unable to weigh; therefore unwilling to buy certificates; frontier merchants distressed, therefore sought permission to weigh Hedong salt.
translations.idiomatic: In the late Jiajing years production-cost salt was in force; some interior merchants waited years without weighing, grew unwilling to buy certificates, and frontier merchants, hard pressed, petitioned to weigh Hedong salt instead.

sentences.zh: 河鹽者，不上廩囷，在河逕自超掣，易支而獲利捷。

translations.literal: Hedong salt: does not enter granary stores, on the river route directly advances weighing; easy to disburse and quick profit.
translations.idiomatic: Hedong salt did not pass through granary stores but could be weighed and taken directly on the river route, making disbursement easy and profit swift.

sentences.zh: 河鹽行，則守支存積者愈久，而內商亦困，引價彌賤。

translations.literal: Once Hedong salt circulated, those waiting for reserve-stock disbursement waited even longer, interior merchants were also distressed, and certificate prices grew ever cheaper.
translations.idiomatic: Once Hedong salt was in circulation, merchants waiting for reserve-stock disbursement waited even longer, interior merchants were squeezed harder, and certificate prices sank lower still.

sentences.zh: 於是奸人專以收買邊引為事，名曰囤戶，告掣河鹽，坐規厚利。

translations.literal: Thereupon schemers made buying frontier certificates their sole business, called hoarders, petitioning to weigh Hedong salt, sitting to plot thick profit.
translations.idiomatic: Schemers then made a specialty of buying up frontier certificates. Known as hoarders, they petitioned for the right to weigh Hedong salt, intending to reap large profits.

sentences.zh: 時復議於正鹽外附帶餘鹽，以抵工本之數，囤戶因得賤賣餘鹽而貴售之，邊商與內商愈困矣。

translations.literal: At the time they again debated attaching surplus salt outside regular salt to offset production-cost amounts; hoarders thus could cheaply sell surplus salt and expensively sell it; frontier and interior merchants grew even more distressed.
translations.idiomatic: Officials again debated allowing surplus salt to be bundled with regular salt to cover production costs. Hoarders could then sell surplus salt cheaply and regular salt at high prices, deepening the distress of frontier and interior merchants alike.

sentences.zh: 隆慶二年，屯鹽都御史龐尚鵬疏言：「邊商報中，內商守支，事本相須。

translations.literal: Longqing second year, salt censor Pang Shangpeng memorialized: "Frontier merchants report tenders, interior merchants wait for disbursement—the affairs fundamentally depend on each other.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Longqing, salt censor Pang Shangpeng memorialized: "Frontier merchants tender certificates and interior merchants wait for disbursement; the two sides fundamentally depend on each other.

sentences.zh: 但內商安坐，邊商遠輸，勞逸不均，故掣河鹽者以惠邊商也。

translations.literal: But interior merchants sit at ease, frontier merchants transport from afar; labor and ease are uneven—therefore weighing Hedong salt is to benefit frontier merchants.
translations.idiomatic: Yet interior merchants sat at ease while frontier merchants hauled grain from afar, so the burden was uneven. Weighing Hedong salt was meant to favor frontier merchants.

sentences.zh: 然河鹽既行，淮鹽必滯，內商無所得利，則邊商之引不售。

translations.literal: Yet once Hedong salt circulates, Huai salt must stagnate; interior merchants gain no profit, then frontier merchants' certificates do not sell.
translations.idiomatic: Yet once Hedong salt circulated, Huai salt was bound to pile up; if interior merchants saw no profit, frontier merchants could not sell their certificates.

sentences.zh: 今宜停掣河鹽，但別邊商引價，自見引及起紙關引到司勘合，別為三等，定銀若干。

translations.literal: Now should stop weighing Hedong salt, but separately set frontier merchant certificate prices: from visible certificate through paper initiation, transport certificate arrival at office verification—separately three grades, fix silver so much.
translations.idiomatic: The court should now halt Hedong salt weighing and instead set separate prices for frontier certificates, graded in three tiers from presentation of the certificate through paper initiation, transport clearance, and office verification, each with a fixed silver rate.

sentences.zh: 邊商倉鈔已到，內商不得留難。

translations.literal: When frontier merchants' warehouse notes have arrived, interior merchants must not obstruct.
translations.idiomatic: Once a frontier merchant's warehouse receipt had arrived, interior merchants must not delay disbursement.

sentences.zh: 蓋河鹽停則淮鹽速行，引價定則開中自多，邊商內商各得其願矣。」

translations.literal: For stopping Hedong salt then Huai salt quickly circulates; fixing certificate prices then kaizhong naturally increases; frontier and interior merchants each get their wish."
translations.idiomatic: Stopping Hedong salt would let Huai salt move quickly again; fixing certificate prices would revive kaizhong tenders; frontier and interior merchants would each get what they wanted.

sentences.zh: 帝從之。

translations.literal: The emperor followed it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved the proposal.

sentences.zh: 四年，御史李學詩議罷官買餘鹽。

translations.literal: Fourth year, censor Li Xueshi proposed abolishing government purchase of surplus salt.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year, censor Li Xueshi proposed abolishing the government purchase of surplus salt.

sentences.zh: 報可。

translations.literal: Report approved.
translations.idiomatic: Approval was granted.

sentences.zh: 是時廣西古田平，巡撫都御史殷正茂請官出資本買廣東鹽，至桂林發賣，七萬餘包可獲利二萬二千有奇。

translations.literal: At this time Guangxi Gutian was pacified; grand coordinator Yin Zhengmao requested government capital buy Guangdong salt, sell at Guilin, seventy thousand-odd packages could gain profit twenty-two thousand-odd.
translations.idiomatic: At this time Gutian in Guangxi had been pacified, and grand coordinator Yin Zhengmao proposed that the government invest capital to buy Guangdong salt and sell it at Guilin, yielding a profit of a little over twenty-two thousand taels on more than seventy thousand packages.

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: Followed.
translations.idiomatic: The proposal was approved.

sentences.zh: 自嘉靖初，復常股四分，存積六分之制。

translations.literal: From early Jiajing, restored changgu four parts, cunji six parts system.
translations.idiomatic: From the early Jiajing reign the four-six split between the regular allotment and reserve stock was restored.

sentences.zh: 後因各邊多故，常股、存積並開，淮額歲課七十萬五千餘引，又增各邊新引歲二十萬。

translations.literal: Later because each frontier had many troubles, changgu and cunji both opened; Huai quota annual levy seven hundred five thousand-odd certificates, also added each frontier new certificates annually two hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Later, with frequent emergencies on the frontiers, both the regular allotment and reserve stock were opened; the Huai quota stood at a little over 705,000 certificates a year, with another 200,000 new frontier certificates added annually.

sentences.zh: 萬歷時，以大工搜遠年違沒廢引六十餘萬，胥出課額之外，無正鹽，止令商買補餘鹽。

translations.literal: Wanli times, for great works searched long-years lapsed confiscated voided certificates six hundred thousand-odd, all outside quota levy, no regular salt, only ordered merchants buy supplement surplus salt.
translations.idiomatic: Under Wanli, major construction projects prompted a search that turned up more than 600,000 long-lapsed, confiscated, and voided certificates, all outside the official quota; with no regular salt available, merchants were told only to buy surplus salt to make up the shortfall.

sentences.zh: 餘鹽久盡，惟計引重科，加煎飛派而已。

translations.literal: Surplus salt long exhausted, only counted certificate weight to levy extra, added boiling and arbitrary apportionment.
translations.idiomatic: Once surplus salt was exhausted, the government merely levied by certificate weight, added extra boiling quotas, and imposed arbitrary surcharges.

sentences.zh: 時兩淮引價餘銀百二十餘萬增至百四十五萬，新引日益，正引日壅。

translations.literal: Then Lianghuai certificate price surplus silver one million two hundred thousand-odd increased to one million four hundred fifty thousand; new certificates daily increased, regular certificates daily blocked.
translations.idiomatic: Lianghuai surplus silver on certificate prices rose from a little over 1.2 million taels to 1.45 million; new certificates multiplied while regular certificates piled up unsold.

sentences.zh: 千戶尹英請配賣沒官鹽，可得銀六萬兩。

translations.literal: Company commander Yin Ying requested allotted sale of confiscated salt, could get silver sixty thousand taels.
translations.idiomatic: Company commander Yin Ying proposed selling off confiscated salt by allotment, which he said would yield 60,000 taels of silver.

sentences.zh: 大學士張位等爭之。

translations.literal: Grand Secretaries Zhang Wei and others disputed it.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Secretaries Zhang Wei and others objected.

sentences.zh: 二十六年，以鴻臚寺主簿田應璧奏，命中官魯保鬻兩淮沒官餘鹽。

translations.literal: Twenty-sixth year, on Honglu Temple registrar Tian Yingbi's memorial, ordered eunuch Lu Bao sell Lianghuai confiscated surplus salt.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-sixth year, on a memorial from Honglu Temple registrar Tian Yingbi, the emperor ordered the eunuch Lu Bao to sell Lianghuai's confiscated surplus salt.

sentences.zh: 給事中包見捷極陳利害。

translations.literal: Supervising Secretary Bao Jianjie intensely stated benefits and harms.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising Secretary Bao Jianjie laid out the full costs and benefits in strong terms.

sentences.zh: 不聽。

translations.literal: Did not listen.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor refused to heed him.

sentences.zh: 保既視事，遂議開存積鹽。

translations.literal: Once Bao took office, then proposed opening reserve stock salt.
translations.idiomatic: Once Lu Bao took up his post, he proposed opening reserve-stock salt.

sentences.zh: 戶部尚書楊俊民言：「明旨核沒官鹽，而存積非沒官也。

translations.literal: Minister of Revenue Yang Junmin said: "Clear edict verified confiscated salt, but reserve stock is not confiscated.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Revenue Yang Junmin said, "The clear imperial order was to audit confiscated salt, but reserve stock is not confiscated property.

sentences.zh: 額外加增，必虧正課。

translations.literal: Beyond quota added increase, must harm regular quota.
translations.idiomatic: Any increase beyond the quota must come at the expense of regular revenue.

sentences.zh: 保奏不可從。」

translations.literal: Bao's memorial cannot be followed."
translations.idiomatic: Lu Bao's proposal should not be adopted.

sentences.zh: 御史馬從騁亦爭之。

translations.literal: Censor Ma Congcheng also disputed it.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Ma Congcheng objected as well.

sentences.zh: 俱不聽。

translations.literal: All not listened to.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor refused all objections.

sentences.zh: 保乃開存積八萬引，引重五百七十斤，越次超掣，壓正鹽不行。

translations.literal: Bao then opened reserve stock eighty thousand certificates, certificate weight five hundred seventy jin, skipping order advance weighing, suppressed regular salt from circulating.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Bao then opened 80,000 reserve-stock certificates of 570 jin each, weighed them out of turn ahead of regular stock, and blocked regular salt from circulating.

sentences.zh: 商民大擾，而奸人蜂起。

translations.literal: Merchants and people greatly disturbed, schemers swarmed forth.
translations.idiomatic: Merchants and common people were thrown into turmoil, and schemers swarmed forth.

sentences.zh: 董璉、吳應麒等爭言鹽利。

translations.literal: Dong Lian, Wu Yingqi and others competed to speak of salt profits.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Lian, Wu Yingqi, and others competed to tout the profits to be made from salt.

sentences.zh: 山西、福建諸稅監皆領鹽課矣。

translations.literal: Shanxi, Fujian tax commissioners all took charge of salt levies.
translations.idiomatic: Tax commissioners in Shanxi and Fujian all took charge of salt revenues as well.

sentences.zh: 百戶高時夏奏浙、閩餘鹽歲可變價三十萬兩，巡撫金學會勘奏皆罔。

translations.literal: Company commander Gao Shixia memorialized Zhe, Min surplus salt annually could be converted to price three hundred thousand taels; grand coordinator Jin Xue investigated and memorialized all false.
translations.idiomatic: Company commander Gao Shixia memorialized that surplus salt in Zhejiang and Fujian could be sold annually for 300,000 taels; grand coordinator Jin Xue investigated and reported that the claim was entirely false.

sentences.zh: 疏入不省。

translations.literal: Memorial entered, not examined.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was submitted but drew no response.

sentences.zh: 於是福建解銀萬三千兩有奇，浙江解三萬七千兩有奇，借名苛斂，商困引壅。

translations.literal: Thereupon Fujian delivered silver thirteen thousand-odd taels, Zhejiang delivered thirty-seven thousand-odd taels, borrowing names harshly levied; merchants distressed, certificates blocked.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Fujian delivered a little over 13,000 taels and Zhejiang a little over 37,000, levied under pretexts of harsh exaction; merchants were hard pressed and certificates piled up unsold.

sentences.zh: 戶部尚書趙世卿指其害由保，因言：「額外多取一分，則正課少一分，而國計愈絀，請悉罷無名浮課。」

translations.literal: Minister of Revenue Zhao Shiqing pointed harm came from Bao, therefore said: "Beyond quota each extra part taken, regular quota one part less, state revenue increasingly deficient—request entirely abolish nameless floating levies."
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Revenue Zhao Shiqing traced the harm to Lu Bao and said, "Every extra levy beyond the quota reduces regular revenue by the same amount and leaves the state treasury ever shorter; I ask that all unscheduled floating levies be abolished.

sentences.zh: 不報。

translations.literal: No reply.
translations.idiomatic: No reply was given.

sentences.zh: 三十四年夏至明年春，正額逋百餘萬，保亦惶懼，請罷存積引鹽。

translations.literal: Thirty-fourth year summer to next year spring, regular quota arrears over a million; Bao also fearful, requested abolish reserve stock certificate salt.
translations.idiomatic: From the summer of the thirty-fourth year to the following spring, arrears on the regular quota exceeded a million taels; Lu Bao, now alarmed, asked to abolish reserve-stock certificate salt.

sentences.zh: 保尋死。

translations.literal: Bao soon died.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Bao soon died.

sentences.zh: 有旨罷之，而引斤不能減矣。

translations.literal: Had edict to abolish it, but certificate weight could not be reduced.
translations.idiomatic: An edict abolished the practice, but the increased weight per certificate could not be rolled back.

sentences.zh: 李太后薨，帝用遺誥蠲各運司浮課，商困稍蘇，而舊引壅滯。

translations.literal: Empress Dowager Li died; emperor used testament edict remit each transport office floating levies; merchant distress slightly revived, but old certificates still blocked.
translations.idiomatic: After Empress Dowager Li died, the emperor used her testamentary edict to remit the floating levies of every transport office; merchant distress eased somewhat, but old certificates remained blocked.

sentences.zh: 戶部上鹽法十議，正行見引，附銷積引，以疏通之。

translations.literal: Ministry of Revenue submitted ten salt law proposals: prioritize current certificates, attach clearing accumulated certificates, to unblock them.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of Revenue submitted ten proposals on salt law: current certificates were to circulate first, with accumulated old certificates cleared alongside them, so as to unblock the system.

sentences.zh: 巡鹽御史龍遇奇立鹽政綱法，以舊引附見引行，淮南編為十綱，淮北編為十四綱，計十餘年，則舊引盡行。

translations.literal: Salt censor Long Yuqi established salt administration gang system: old certificates attached to current certificates for circulation; south Huai organized into ten gangs, north Huai into fourteen gangs; counting ten-odd years, then old certificates all circulate.
translations.idiomatic: Salt censor Long Yuqi established a gang system for salt administration, attaching old certificates to current ones for circulation: south of the Huai was organized into ten gangs and north of the Huai into fourteen, so that within a little over ten years all old certificates would be cleared.

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: Followed.
translations.idiomatic: The proposal was approved.

sentences.zh: 天啟時，言利者恣蒐括，務增引超掣。

translations.literal: Tianqi times, profit-seekers freely scraped and levied, striving to increase certificates and advance weighing.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Tianqi emperor, profit-seekers scraped and levied at will, striving to increase certificates and rush them through weighing out of turn.

sentences.zh: 魏忠賢黨郭興治、崔呈秀等，巧立名目以取之，所入無算。

translations.literal: Wei Zhongxian's faction Guo Xingzhi, Cui Chengxiu and others, cleverly established names to take revenue, income beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Zhongxian's followers Guo Xingzhi, Cui Chengxiu, and others devised new pretexts to extract revenue, and the sums they collected were beyond reckoning.

sentences.zh: 論者比之絕流而漁。

translations.literal: Commentators compared it to draining the stream to fish.
translations.idiomatic: Commentators compared the practice to draining a stream to catch its fish.

sentences.zh: 崇禎中，給事中黃承昊條上鹽政，頗欲有所釐革。

translations.literal: Chongzhen period, supervising secretary Huang Chenghao itemized salt administration, quite wishing to make reforms.
translations.idiomatic: In the Chongzhen reign, supervising secretary Huang Chenghao submitted a detailed plan for salt administration and sought substantial reforms.

sentences.zh: 是時兵餉方大絀，不能行也。

translations.literal: At this time military pay greatly deficient, could not be implemented.
translations.idiomatic: Military pay was severely short at the time, and the reforms could not be carried out.

sentences.zh: 初，諸王府則就近地支鹽，官民戶口食鹽皆計口納鈔，自行關支。

translations.literal: Initially, princely establishments disbursed salt from nearby places; official and common households' salt consumption all counted mouths paying paper money, themselves conducting disbursement.
translations.idiomatic: At first, princely establishments drew salt from nearby depots, while officials and commoners paid paper notes per capita for household salt and collected it themselves.

sentences.zh: 而官吏食鹽多冒增口數，有一官支二千餘斤，一吏支五百餘斤者。

translations.literal: But officials and clerks' salt mostly falsely increased mouth counts; some one official drew two thousand-odd jin, one clerk five hundred-odd jin.
translations.idiomatic: Officials and clerks often inflated their household counts; one official might draw more than 2,000 jin and one clerk more than 500.

sentences.zh: 乃限吏典不得過十口，文武官不過三十口；

translations.literal: Then limited clerical staff no more than ten mouths, civil and military officials no more than thirty mouths;
translations.idiomatic: Limits were then set: clerical staff could claim no more than ten mouths, and civil and military officials no more than thirty;

sentences.zh: 大口鈔十二貫支鹽十二斤，小口半之。

translations.literal: Large mouth paper money twelve guan disbursed salt twelve jin, small mouth half.
translations.idiomatic: a large mouth received twelve jin of salt for twelve guan in paper notes, and a small mouth half that amount.

sentences.zh: 景泰三年始以鹽折給官吏俸糧，以百四十斤當米一石。

translations.literal: Jingtai third year first used salt converted to pay officials' salaries, one hundred forty jin equivalent to one shi of rice.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Jingtai, salt was first used in lieu of officials' grain salaries, with 140 jin taken as equivalent to one shi of rice.

sentences.zh: 京官歲遣吏下場，恣為奸利。

translations.literal: Capital officials annually sent clerks down to salt fields, freely making corrupt profits.
translations.idiomatic: Capital officials sent clerks down to the salt fields every year to squeeze illicit profits.

sentences.zh: 錦衣吏益暴，率聯巨艦私販，有司不能詰。

translations.literal: Brocade Guard clerks especially violent, leading linked great ships in private sales; local officials could not investigate.
translations.idiomatic: Clerks of the Brocade Guard were especially brazen, linking great ships to smuggle salt privately, and local officials could not stop them.

sentences.zh: 巡鹽御史乃定百司食鹽數，攟束以給吏，禁毋下場。

translations.literal: Salt censor then fixed all offices' salt amounts, bundled and issued to clerks, forbade going down to fields.
translations.idiomatic: The salt censor then fixed each office's salt allotment, bundled it for delivery to clerks, and forbade sending men down to the salt fields.

sentences.zh: 納鈔、僦輓，費無所出，吏多亡。

translations.literal: Paying paper money, hiring transport, costs nowhere to come from, many clerks fled.
translations.idiomatic: With no way to cover the cost of paper notes and hired transport, many clerks simply disappeared.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖中，吏部郎中陸光祖言於尚書嚴訥，疏請革之。

translations.literal: Jiajing period, Ministry of Personnel director Lu Guangzu spoke to Minister Yan Ne, memorialized requesting abolish it.
translations.idiomatic: During Jiajing, Ministry of Personnel director Lu Guangzu spoke with Minister Yan Ne and memorialized to abolish the practice.

sentences.zh: 自後百司停支食鹽，惟戶部及十三道御史歲支如故。

translations.literal: From then all offices stopped salt disbursement; only Ministry of Revenue and thirteen circuits of censors annually received as before.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter every office stopped drawing salt except the Ministry of Revenue and the censors of the thirteen circuits, who continued to receive their annual allotments as before.

sentences.zh: 軍民計口納鈔者，浙江月納米三升，賣鹽一斤，而商賈持鹽赴官，官為斂散，追徵之急過於租賦。

translations.literal: Soldiers and civilians counting mouths paying paper money: Zhejiang monthly paid three sheng rice, sold one jin salt; but merchants bringing salt to government, government collected and dispersed, collection urgency exceeded land tax.
translations.idiomatic: Where soldiers and civilians paid per capita in paper notes, Zhejiang required three sheng of rice a month and sold one jin of salt; yet when merchants brought salt to the government for distribution, collection was pursued more ruthlessly than land tax.

sentences.zh: 正統時，從給事中鮑輝言，令民自買食鹽於商，罷納米令，且鬻十斤以下者勿以私鹽論，而鹽鈔不除。

translations.literal: Zhengtong period, following supervising secretary Bao Hui's words, ordered people buy salt themselves from merchants, abolished rice-payment order, and selling under ten jin not treated as private salt, but salt paper money not removed.
translations.idiomatic: In the Zhengtong reign, on the advice of supervising secretary Bao Hui, people were allowed to buy salt directly from merchants, the rice-payment order was abolished, and sales under ten jin were not treated as private salt, though salt paper notes were not abolished.

sentences.zh: 後條鞭法行，遂編入正賦。

translations.literal: Later single-whip method implemented, then compiled into regular levy.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when the single-whip tax reform took effect, the charge was folded into the regular land tax.

sentences.zh: 巡鹽之官，洪、永時，嘗一再命御史視鹽課。

translations.literal: Salt-inspection officials: Hongwu, Yongle times, once or twice ordered censors oversee salt levies.
translations.idiomatic: Salt inspectors: in the Hongwu and Yongle reigns, censors were once or twice ordered to oversee salt revenues.

sentences.zh: 正統元年始命侍郎何文淵、王佐，副都御史硃與言提督兩淮、長蘆、兩浙鹽課，命中官御史同往。

translations.literal: Zhengtong first year first ordered Vice Ministers He Wenyuan, Wang Zuo, Vice Censor-in-Chief Zhu Yuyan to supervise Lianghuai, Changlu, Liangzhe salt levies, ordered eunuchs and censors go together.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Zhengtong, Vice Ministers He Wenyuan and Wang Zuo and Vice Censor-in-Chief Zhu Yuyan were first appointed to supervise salt revenues in Lianghuai, Changlu, and Liangzhe, with eunuchs and censors sent along with them.

sentences.zh: 未幾，以鹽法已清，下敕召還。

translations.literal: Before long, because salt law already clear, issued edict to recall.
translations.idiomatic: Before long, once the salt system had been straightened out, an edict recalled them.

sentences.zh: 後遂令御史視鹺，依巡按例，歲更代以為常。

translations.literal: Later then ordered censors oversee salt, following circuit inspection precedent, yearly rotation became standard.
translations.idiomatic: Censors were later put in charge of salt inspection on the model of circuit inspection, with annual rotation becoming the rule.

sentences.zh: 十一年以山東諸鹽場隸長蘆巡鹽御史。

translations.literal: Eleventh year placed Shandong salt fields under Changlu salt censor.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year, Shandong's salt fields were placed under the Changlu salt censor.

sentences.zh: 十四年命副都御史耿九疇清理兩淮鹽法。

translations.literal: Fourteenth year ordered Vice Censor-in-Chief Geng Jiuchou to rectify Lianghuai salt law.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year, Vice Censor-in-Chief Geng Jiuchou was ordered to rectify the Lianghuai salt system.

sentences.zh: 成化中，特遣中官王允中、僉都御史高明整治兩淮鹽法。

translations.literal: Chenghua period, specially dispatched eunuch Wang Yunzhong, Vice Censor-in-Chief Gao Ming to reorganize Lianghuai salt law.
translations.idiomatic: During Chenghua, the eunuch Wang Yunzhong and Vice Censor-in-Chief Gao Ming were specially dispatched to reorganize Lianghuai salt policy.

sentences.zh: 明請增設副使一人，判官二人。

translations.literal: Gao requested adding one vice commissioner, two magistrate assistants.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Ming requested one additional vice commissioner and two magistrate assistants.

sentences.zh: 孝宗初，鹽法壞，戶部尚書李敏請簡風憲大臣清理，乃命戶部侍郎李嗣於兩淮，刑部侍郎彭韶於兩浙，俱兼都御史，賜敕遣之。

translations.literal: Early Xiaozong, salt law broken; Minister Li Min requested select integrity grandee to rectify; then ordered Vice Minister Li Si at Lianghuai, Vice Minister Peng Shao at Liangzhe, all concurrently censor-in-chief, granted edict and dispatched.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Xiaozong reign the salt system had broken down; Minister of Revenue Li Min asked that a senior integrity official be chosen to set it right, and Vice Ministers Li Si and Peng Shao were sent to Lianghuai and Liangzhe respectively, each concurrently serving as censor-in-chief with an imperial commission.

sentences.zh: 弘治十四年，僉都御史王璟督理兩淮鹽法。

translations.literal: Hongzhi fourteenth year, Vice Censor-in-Chief Wang Jing supervised Lianghuai salt law.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year of Hongzhi, Vice Censor-in-Chief Wang Jing supervised Lianghuai salt policy.

sentences.zh: 正德二年，兩淮則僉都御史王瓊，閩、浙則僉都御史張憲。

translations.literal: Zhengde second year, Lianghuai had Vice Censor-in-Chief Wang Qiong, Min-Zhe had Vice Censor-in-Chief Zhang Xian.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Zhengde, Lianghuai was overseen by Vice Censor-in-Chief Wang Qiong and Fujian-Zhejiang by Vice Censor-in-Chief Zhang Xian.

sentences.zh: 後惟兩淮賦重，時遣大臣。

translations.literal: Later only Lianghuai levy heavy, periodically dispatched grand ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Later only Lianghuai bore a heavy levy, and senior ministers were periodically dispatched there.

sentences.zh: 十年，則刑部侍郎藍章。

translations.literal: Tenth year, then Vice Minister Lan Zhang.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year it was Vice Minister Lan Zhang.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖七年，則副都御史黃臣。

translations.literal: Jiajing seventh year, then Vice Censor-in-Chief Huang Chen.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of Jiajing, Vice Censor-in-Chief Huang Chen.

sentences.zh: 三十二年，則副都御史王紳。

translations.literal: Thirty-second year, then Vice Censor-in-Chief Wang Shen.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-second year, Vice Censor-in-Chief Wang Shen.

sentences.zh: 至三十九年，特命副都御史鄢懋卿總理四運司，事權尤重。

translations.literal: Reaching thirty-ninth year, specially ordered Vice Censor-in-Chief Yan Maoqing to oversee four transport offices, authority especially weighty.
translations.idiomatic: By the thirty-ninth year, Vice Censor-in-Chief Yan Maoqing was specially appointed to oversee all four transport offices, with authority heavier than ever.

sentences.zh: 自隆慶二年，副都御史龐尚鵬總理兩淮、長蘆、山東三運司後，遂無特遣大臣之事。

translations.literal: From Longqing second year, after Vice Censor-in-Chief Pang Shangpeng overseaw Lianghuai, Changlu, Shandong three transport offices, then no specially dispatched grand ministers.
translations.idiomatic: From the second year of Longqing, after Vice Censor-in-Chief Pang Shangpeng had overseen the three transport offices of Lianghuai, Changlu, and Shandong, no senior minister was specially dispatched again.

sentences.zh: 番人嗜乳酪，不得茶，則困以病。

translations.literal: Frontier peoples fond of dairy; without tea, then distressed until illness.
translations.idiomatic: Frontier peoples lived on dairy foods, and without tea they grew sick with deprivation.

sentences.zh: 故唐、宋以來，行以茶易馬法，用制羌、戎，而明制尤密。

translations.literal: Therefore from Tang, Song, implemented tea-for-horses law, to control Qiang and Rong; Ming system especially strict.
translations.idiomatic: From Tang and Song times onward the tea-for-horses system had been used to control the Qiang and Rong peoples, and under the Ming it was enforced with especial rigor.

sentences.zh: 有官茶，有商茶，皆貯邊易馬。

translations.literal: There is official tea, merchant tea, all stored at frontier to trade for horses.
translations.idiomatic: There was official tea and merchant tea, both stored on the frontier to be traded for horses.

sentences.zh: 官茶間徵課鈔，商茶輸課略如鹽制。

translations.literal: Official tea occasionally levied paper money; merchant tea paid levies roughly like salt system.
translations.idiomatic: Official tea was occasionally taxed in paper notes, while merchant tea paid levies much like the salt system.

sentences.zh: 初，太祖令商人於產茶地買茶，納錢請引。

translations.literal: Initially, Taizu ordered merchants at tea-producing places buy tea, pay money request certificate.
translations.idiomatic: At first the Taizu emperor ordered merchants to buy tea in producing regions, pay a fee, and obtain a certificate.

sentences.zh: 引茶百斤，輸錢二百，不及引曰畸零，別置由帖給之。

translations.literal: Certificate tea hundred jin, pay money two hundred; not reaching certificate called odd lot, separately issued slip.
translations.idiomatic: A full certificate covered one hundred jin of tea for a payment of two hundred cash; amounts below a full certificate, called odd lots, were issued separate slips.

sentences.zh: 無由、引及茶引相離者，人得告捕。

translations.literal: Without slip, certificate, and tea-certificate separated, anyone may report and arrest.
translations.idiomatic: Anyone lacking a slip or certificate, or carrying tea apart from its certificate, could be reported and arrested.

sentences.zh: 置茶局批驗所，稱較茶引不相當，即為私茶。

translations.literal: Established tea bureau inspection stations; weighing tea and certificate not matching, then private tea.
translations.idiomatic: Tea bureaus and inspection stations were set up; if the weighed tea did not match the certificate, it was treated as private tea.

sentences.zh: 凡犯私茶者，與私鹽同罪。

translations.literal: All who violate private tea, same crime as private salt.
translations.idiomatic: Violators of the private-tea ban were punished like private-salt smugglers.

sentences.zh: 私茶出境，與關隘不譏者，並論死。

translations.literal: Private tea leaving frontier, and pass officials not inspecting—both punished by death.
translations.idiomatic: Smuggling private tea beyond the frontier, and pass officials who failed to inspect it, were both punishable by death.

sentences.zh: 後又定茶引一道，輸錢千，照茶百斤；

translations.literal: Later again fixed tea certificate one document, pay money one thousand, corresponding to tea hundred jin;
translations.idiomatic: Later a tea certificate was fixed at one thousand cash for one hundred jin of tea;

sentences.zh: 茶由一道，輸錢六百，照茶六十斤。

translations.literal: Tea slip one document, pay money six hundred, corresponding to tea sixty jin.
translations.idiomatic: and a tea slip at six hundred cash for sixty jin.

sentences.zh: 既，又令納鈔，每引由一道，納鈔一貫。

translations.literal: Then again ordered pay paper money, each certificate or slip one document, pay paper money one guan.
translations.idiomatic: Payment was later changed to paper notes, one guan per certificate or slip.

sentences.zh: 洪武初，定令：凡賣茶之地，令宣課司三十取一。

translations.literal: Hongwu early, fixed regulation: all tea-selling places, ordered Revenue Promotion Office take one from thirty.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Hongwu a rule was set that wherever tea was sold, the local Revenue Promotion Office should take one part in thirty.

sentences.zh: 四年，戶部言：「陝西漢中、金州、石泉、漢陰、平利、西鄉諸縣，茶園四十五頃，茶八十六萬餘株。

translations.literal: Fourth year, Ministry said: "Shaanxi Hanzhong, Jinzhou, Shiquan, Hanyin, Pingli, Xixiang counties, tea gardens forty-five qing, tea eight hundred sixty thousand-odd plants.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year the Ministry reported: "In Hanzhong, Jinzhou, Shiquan, Hanyin, Pingli, and Xixiang in Shaanxi there are forty-five qing of tea gardens with more than 860,000 tea plants.

sentences.zh: 四川巴茶三百十五戶，茶二百三十八萬餘株。

translations.literal: Sichuan Ba tea three hundred fifteen households, tea two million three hundred eighty thousand-odd plants.
translations.idiomatic: In Sichuan, 315 Ba-tea households tend more than 2.38 million plants.

sentences.zh: 宜定令每十株官取其一。

translations.literal: Should fix regulation: every ten plants government takes one.
translations.idiomatic: It is appropriate to fix a rule that the government take one plant in ten.

sentences.zh: 無主茶園，令軍士薅採，十取其八，以易番馬。」

translations.literal: Ownerless tea gardens, order soldiers pluck harvest, take eight from ten, to trade for frontier horses."
translations.idiomatic: In ownerless tea gardens, soldiers were to harvest the crop, keeping eight plants in ten to trade for frontier horses.

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: The emperor approved it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved the proposal.

sentences.zh: 於是諸產茶地設茶課司，定稅額，陝西二萬六千斤有奇，四川一百萬斤。

translations.literal: Thereupon at all tea-producing places established Tea Tax Offices, fixed tax quotas: Shaanxi 26,000-odd jin, Sichuan one million jin.
translations.idiomatic: Tea Tax Offices were then established in every tea-producing region, with fixed quotas of a little over 26,000 jin for Shaanxi and one million jin for Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 設茶馬司於秦、洮、河、雅渚州，自碉門、黎、雅抵朵甘、烏思藏，行茶之地五千餘里。

translations.literal: Established Tea and Horse Offices at Qin, Tao, He, and Yazhu; from Diaomen, Li, and Ya reaching Do-kham and U-Tsang, the distance over which tea was transported exceeded five thousand li.
translations.idiomatic: Tea and Horse Offices were set up at Qin, Tao, He, and Yazhu, and tea was carried more than five thousand li from Diaomen, Li, and Ya westward as far as Do-kham and U-Tsang.

sentences.zh: 山後歸德諸州，西方諸部落，無不以馬售者。

translations.literal: The Guide prefectures beyond the mountains and all the western tribes — none did not come to sell horses.
translations.idiomatic: From the Guide prefectures beyond the mountains to the western tribes, all came to sell horses.

sentences.zh: 碉門、永寧、筠、連所產茶，名曰剪刀粗葉，惟西番用之，而商販未嘗出境。

translations.literal: Tea produced at Diaomen, Yongning, Jun, and Lian, called Scissors Coarse Leaf; only the western tribes used it, and merchants had never exported it across the border.
translations.idiomatic: Tea from Diaomen, Yongning, Jun, and Lian, known as Scissors Coarse Leaf, was used only by western tribes, and merchants had never before exported it across the border.

sentences.zh: 四川茶鹽都轉運使言：「宜別立茶局，徵其稅，易紅纓、氈衫、米、布、椒、蠟以資國用。

translations.literal: The Sichuan Commissioner of Tea and Salt said: "It is appropriate to establish separate tea bureaus, levy their tax, and exchange for red tassels, felt garments, rice, cloth, pepper, and wax to supply state revenue.
translations.idiomatic: The Sichuan Commissioner of Tea and Salt reported: "Separate tea bureaus should be established to levy taxes and trade for red tassels, felt jackets, rice, cloth, pepper, and wax to supply state revenue.

sentences.zh: 而居民所收之茶，依江南給引販賣法，公私兩便。」

translations.literal: As for tea gathered by local residents, follow the Jiangnan method of issuing permits for sale, benefiting both public revenue and private trade."
translations.idiomatic: Tea gathered by local residents should be sold under the Jiangnan system of issued permits, benefiting both public revenue and private trade.

sentences.zh: 於是永甯、成都、筠、連皆設茶局矣。

translations.literal: Thereupon Yongning, Chengdu, Jun, and Lian all established tea bureaus.
translations.idiomatic: Yongning, Chengdu, Jun, and Lian accordingly all gained tea bureaus.

sentences.zh: 川人故以茶易毛布、毛纓諸物以償茶課。

translations.literal: Sichuan people had long used tea to exchange for felt cloth, felt tassels, and other goods to pay their tea tax.
translations.idiomatic: Sichuan people had long traded tea for felt cloth, felt tassels, and the like to meet their tea tax obligations.

sentences.zh: 自定課額，立倉收貯，專用以市馬，民不敢私採，課額每虧，民多賠納。

translations.literal: Once tax quotas were fixed and warehouses established to store tea exclusively for horse purchases, the people dared not pick tea privately; quotas were often unmet, and many had to pay make-up levies.
translations.idiomatic: Once quotas were fixed and warehouses set up to store tea solely for horse purchases, the people dared not pick tea privately; quotas were often unmet, and many had to pay make-up levies.

sentences.zh: 四川布政司以為言，乃聽民採摘，與番易貨。

translations.literal: When the Sichuan Provincial Administration Commission raised the matter, the people were then permitted to harvest tea and trade goods with the frontier tribes.
translations.idiomatic: When the Sichuan Provincial Administration Commission raised the matter, the people were allowed to harvest tea and trade with the frontier tribes.

sentences.zh: 又詔天全六番司民，免其徭役，專令蒸烏茶易馬。

translations.literal: An edict also exempted the people of the Six Fan Offices of Tianquan from corvée and ordered them to devote themselves to steaming black tea for horse trade.
translations.idiomatic: An edict also exempted the people of the Six Fan Offices of Tianquan from corvée and ordered them to devote themselves to steaming black tea for the horse trade.

sentences.zh: 初制，長河西等番商以馬入雅州易茶，由四川嚴州衛入黎州始達。

translations.literal: Under the original arrangement, merchants from Chang River West and other tribes brought horses to Yazhou to trade for tea, reaching Lizhou only after passing through Yanzhou Guard in Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: Under the original arrangement, merchants from Chang River West and other tribes brought horses to Yazhou to trade for tea, entering Lizhou only after passing through Yanzhou Guard in Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 茶馬司定價，馬一匹，茶千八百斤，於碉門茶課司給之。

translations.literal: The Tea and Horse Office fixed the price at one horse for 1,800 jin of tea, issued from the Diaomen Tea Tax Office.
translations.idiomatic: The Tea and Horse Office set the rate at 1,800 jin of tea per horse, issued from the Diaomen Tea Tax Office.

sentences.zh: 番商往復迂遠，而給茶太多。

translations.literal: Tribal merchants traveled a long roundabout route, yet received far too much tea.
translations.idiomatic: Tribal merchants had to travel a long roundabout route, and received far too much tea.

sentences.zh: 嚴州衛以為言，請置茶馬司於嚴州，而改貯碉門茶於其地，且驗馬高下以為茶數。

translations.literal: Yanzhou Guard petitioned to place a Tea and Horse Office at Yanzhou, relocate the tea stored at Diaomen there, and set the tea allowance according to the quality of the horses.
translations.idiomatic: Yanzhou Guard petitioned to place a Tea and Horse Office at Yanzhou, relocate the tea stored at Diaomen there, and set the tea allowance according to the quality of the horses.

sentences.zh: 詔茶馬司仍舊，而定上馬一匹，給茶百二十斤，中七十斤，駒五十斤。

translations.literal: An edict kept the Tea and Horse Office where it was but fixed new rates: 120 jin for a superior horse, 70 for a medium one, and 50 for a foal.
translations.idiomatic: An edict kept the Tea and Horse Office where it was but set new rates: 120 jin for a superior horse, 70 for a medium one, and 50 for a foal.

sentences.zh: 三十年改設秦州茶馬司於西寧，敕右軍都督曰：「近者私茶出境，互市者少，馬日貴而茶日賤，啟番人玩侮之心。

translations.literal: In the thirtieth year the Qinzhou Tea and Horse Office was moved to Xining. The emperor instructed the Right Military Governor: "Private tea has lately been smuggled across the border, few come to the official markets, horses grow costlier while tea grows cheaper, and this invites contempt from the frontier tribes.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirtieth year the Qinzhou Tea and Horse Office was moved to Xining. The emperor instructed the Right Military Governor: "Private tea has lately been smuggled across the border, few come to the official markets, horses grow costlier while tea grows cheaper, and this invites contempt from the frontier tribes.

sentences.zh: 檄秦、蜀二府，發都司官軍於松潘、碉門、黎、雅、河州、臨洮及入西番關口外，巡禁私茶之出境者。」

translations.literal: Send orders to the Qin and Shu regional commands to deploy Regional Command troops to Songpan, Diaomen, Li, Ya, Hezhou, Lintao, and the passes into the western tribes to patrol and stop illicit tea from leaving the border."
translations.idiomatic: Send orders to the Qin and Shu regional commands to deploy troops to Songpan, Diaomen, Li, Ya, Hezhou, Lintao, and the passes into the western tribes to patrol and stop illicit tea from leaving the border.

sentences.zh: 又遣駙馬都尉謝達諭蜀王椿曰：「國家榷茶，本資易馬。

translations.literal: The Prince Consort Commandant Xie Da was also sent to admonish Prince Chun of Shu: "The state's tea monopoly exists chiefly to supply the horse trade.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince Consort Commandant Xie Da was also sent to admonish Prince Chun of Shu: "The state's tea monopoly exists chiefly to supply the horse trade.

sentences.zh: 邊吏失譏，私販出境，惟易紅纓雜物。

translations.literal: Border officials have failed to keep watch; smugglers send tea abroad only to trade for red tassels and petty goods.
translations.idiomatic: Border officials have failed to keep watch; smugglers send tea abroad only to trade for red tassels and petty goods.

sentences.zh: 使番人坐收其利，而馬入中國者少，豈所以制戎狄哉！

translations.literal: The tribes reap the profit effortlessly while few horses reach China — how can this restrain the frontier peoples!
translations.idiomatic: The tribes reap the profit effortlessly while few horses reach China — how can this restrain the frontier peoples!

sentences.zh: 爾其諭布政司、都司，嚴為防禁，毋致失利。」

translations.literal: You must instruct the Provincial Administration Commission and Regional Command to enforce strict prohibitions and not allow the state to suffer this loss."
translations.idiomatic: You must instruct the Provincial Administration Commission and Regional Command to enforce strict prohibitions and not allow the state to suffer this loss."

sentences.zh: 當是時，帝綢繆邊防，用茶易馬，固番人心，且以強中國。

translations.literal: At this time the emperor was deeply attentive to frontier defense: trading tea for horses both solidified tribal loyalty and strengthened the realm.
translations.idiomatic: At this time the emperor was deeply attentive to frontier defense: trading tea for horses both won over the tribes and strengthened the realm.

sentences.zh: 嘗謂戶部尚書鬱新：「用陝西漢中茶三百萬斤，可得馬三萬匹，四川松、茂茶如之。

translations.literal: He once told Minister of Revenue Yu Xin: "Three million jin of Hanzhong tea in Shaanxi could bring thirty thousand horses; tea from Song and Mao in Sichuan would yield the same.
translations.idiomatic: He once told Minister of Revenue Yu Xin: "Three million jin of Hanzhong tea in Shaanxi could bring thirty thousand horses; tea from Song and Mao in Sichuan would yield the same.

sentences.zh: 販鬻之禁，不可不嚴。」

translations.literal: The ban on private sale must be enforced without laxity."
translations.idiomatic: The ban on private sale must be enforced without laxity.

sentences.zh: 以故遣僉都御史鄧文鏗等察川、陝私茶；

translations.literal: Accordingly he dispatched Assistant Censor-in-Chief Deng Wenkeng and others to investigate illicit tea in Sichuan and Shaanxi;
translations.idiomatic: Accordingly he dispatched Assistant Censor-in-Chief Deng Wenkeng and others to investigate illicit tea in Sichuan and Shaanxi;

sentences.zh: 駙馬都尉歐陽倫以私茶坐死。

translations.literal: Prince Consort Commandant Ouyang Lun was executed for smuggling tea.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Consort Commandant Ouyang Lun was executed for smuggling tea.

sentences.zh: 又制金牌信符，命曹國公李景隆齎入番，與諸番要約，篆文上曰「皇帝聖旨」，左曰「合當差發」，右曰「不信者斬」。

translations.literal: Gold credential plaques were also issued, and Duke of Cao Li Jinglong was ordered to carry them into the frontier and covenant with the tribes. The inscriptions read "By Imperial Decree" on the top, "Due Tribute Required" on the left, and "Disobedience Punished by Death" on the right.
translations.idiomatic: Gold credential plaques were also issued, and Duke of Cao Li Jinglong was ordered to carry them into the frontier and covenant with the tribes. The inscriptions read "By Imperial Decree" on the top, "Due Tribute Required" on the left, and "Disobedience Punished by Death" on the right.

sentences.zh: 凡四十一面：洮州火把藏思囊日等族，牌四面，納馬三千五十匹；

translations.literal: There were forty-one plaques in all: for the Huobacang, Sinangri, and other tribes of Taozhou, four plaques requiring 3,050 horses;
translations.idiomatic: There were forty-one plaques in all: for the Huobacang, Sinangri, and other tribes of Taozhou, four plaques requiring 3,050 horses;

sentences.zh: 河州必裏衛西番二十九族，牌二十一面，納馬七千七百五匹；

translations.literal: For the twenty-nine western tribes of Bili Guard in Hezhou, twenty-one plaques requiring 7,755 horses;
translations.idiomatic: for the twenty-nine western tribes of Bili Guard in Hezhou, twenty-one plaques requiring 7,755 horses;

sentences.zh: 西寧曲先、阿端、罕東、安定四衛，巴哇、申中、申藏等族，牌十六面，納馬三千五十匹。

translations.literal: For the four guards of Quxian, Aduan, Handong, and Anding at Xining, together with the Bawa, Shenzhong, Shencang, and other tribes, sixteen plaques requiring 3,050 horses.
translations.idiomatic: and for the four guards of Quxian, Aduan, Handong, and Anding at Xining, together with the Bawa, Shenzhong, Shencang, and other tribes, sixteen plaques requiring 3,050 horses.

sentences.zh: 下號金牌降諸番，上號藏內府以為契，三歲一遣官合符。

translations.literal: The lower halves were issued to the tribes and the upper halves kept in the palace as proof; every three years an official was sent to verify that the halves matched.
translations.idiomatic: The lower halves were issued to the tribes and the upper halves kept in the palace as proof; every three years an official was sent to verify that the halves matched.

sentences.zh: 其通道有二，一出河州，一出碉門，運茶五十餘萬斤，獲馬萬三千八百匹。

translations.literal: There were two routes, one through Hezhou and one through Diaomen; more than 500,000 jin of tea were shipped, and 13,800 horses were obtained.
translations.idiomatic: There were two routes, one through Hezhou and one through Diaomen; more than 500,000 jin of tea were shipped, and 13,800 horses were obtained.

sentences.zh: 太祖之馭番如此。

translations.literal: Such was how Taizu managed the frontier tribes.
translations.idiomatic: Such was how Taizu managed the frontier tribes.

sentences.zh: 永樂中，帝懷柔遠人，遞增茶斤。

translations.literal: Under Yongle the emperor sought to conciliate distant peoples and repeatedly raised the amount of tea offered.
translations.idiomatic: Under Yongle the emperor sought to conciliate distant peoples and repeatedly raised the amount of tea offered.

sentences.zh: 由是市馬者多，而茶不足。

translations.literal: More came to trade horses, but tea ran short.
translations.idiomatic: More came to trade horses, but tea ran short.

sentences.zh: 茶禁亦稍馳，多私出境。

translations.literal: The tea ban also grew slack, and much tea was smuggled across the border.
translations.idiomatic: The tea ban also grew slack, and much tea was smuggled across the border.

sentences.zh: 碉門茶馬司至用茶八萬餘斤，僅易馬七十匹，又多瘦損。

translations.literal: At the Diaomen Tea and Horse Office more than 80,000 jin of tea bought only seventy horses, many of them weak and emaciated.
translations.idiomatic: At the Diaomen Tea and Horse Office more than 80,000 jin of tea bought only seventy horses, many of them weak and emaciated.

sentences.zh: 乃申嚴茶禁，設洮州茶馬司，又設甘肅茶馬司於陝西行都司地。

translations.literal: The tea ban was then tightened, a Tea and Horse Office was set up at Taozhou, and another at Gansu within the Shaanxi military region.
translations.idiomatic: The tea ban was then tightened, a Tea and Horse Office was set up at Taozhou, and another at Gansu within the Shaanxi military region.

sentences.zh: 十三年特遣三御史巡督陝西茶馬。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year three censors were specially sent to oversee the tea-and-horse trade in Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year three censors were specially sent to oversee the tea-and-horse trade in Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 太祖之禁私茶也，自三月至九月，月遣行人四員，巡視河州、臨洮、碉門、黎、雅。

translations.literal: To stop private tea, Taizu from the third to the ninth month sent four envoys each month to inspect Hezhou, Lintao, Diaomen, Li, and Ya.
translations.idiomatic: To stop private tea, Taizu from the third to the ninth month sent four envoys each month to inspect Hezhou, Lintao, Diaomen, Li, and Ya.

sentences.zh: 半年以內，遣二十四員，往來旁午。

translations.literal: Within half a year twenty-four envoys were sent back and forth in constant rotation.
translations.idiomatic: Within half a year twenty-four envoys were sent back and forth in constant rotation.

sentences.zh: 宣德十年，乃定三月一遣。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Xuande this was fixed at one dispatch every third month.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year of Xuande this was fixed at one dispatch every third month.

sentences.zh: 自永樂時停止金牌信符，至是復給。

translations.literal: The gold plaques had been suspended since Yongle; they were now issued again.
translations.idiomatic: The gold plaques had been suspended since Yongle; they were now issued again.

sentences.zh: 未幾，番人為北狄所侵掠，徙居內地，金牌散失。

translations.literal: Before long the tribes, harried by northern raiders, moved inward and the plaques were scattered and lost.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the tribes, harried by northern raiders, moved inward and the plaques were scattered and lost.

sentences.zh: 而茶司亦以茶少，止以漢中茶易馬，且不給金牌，聽其以馬入貢而已。

translations.literal: The Tea Office, finding tea scarce, traded only Hanzhong tea for horses, issued no plaques, and simply allowed the tribes to present horses as tribute.
translations.idiomatic: The Tea Office, finding tea scarce, traded only Hanzhong tea for horses, issued no plaques, and simply allowed the tribes to present horses as tribute.

sentences.zh: 先是，洪武末，置成都、重慶、保寧、播州茶倉四所，令商人納米中茶。

translations.literal: Earlier, at the end of Hongwu, four tea warehouses were established at Chengdu, Chongqing, Baoning, and Bozhou, allowing merchants to pay grain for tea certificates.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, at the end of Hongwu, four tea warehouses were established at Chengdu, Chongqing, Baoning, and Bozhou, allowing merchants to pay grain for tea certificates.

sentences.zh: 宣德中，定官茶百斤，加耗什一。

translations.literal: Under Xuande it was fixed that for every one hundred jin of official tea, a ten-percent allowance for wastage was added.
translations.idiomatic: Under Xuande it was fixed that for every one hundred jin of official tea, a ten-percent allowance for wastage was added.

sentences.zh: 中茶者，自遣人赴甘州、西寧，而支鹽於淮、浙以償費。

translations.literal: Certificate holders sent their own men to Ganzhou and Xining and drew salt in Huai and Zhe to cover costs.
translations.idiomatic: Certificate holders sent their own men to Ganzhou and Xining and drew salt in Huai and Zhe to cover costs.

sentences.zh: 商人恃文憑恣私販，官課數年不完。

translations.literal: Merchants used their documents to smuggle tea freely, and state revenue went uncollected for years.
translations.idiomatic: Merchants used their documents to smuggle tea freely, and state revenue went uncollected for years.

sentences.zh: 正統初，都御史羅亨信言其弊，乃罷運茶支鹽例，令官運如故，以京官總理之。

translations.literal: Early in Zhengtong, Censor-in-Chief Luo Hengxin described these abuses, and the rule allowing transport of tea in exchange for salt was abolished; official transport was restored under a capital official's supervision.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Zhengtong, Censor-in-Chief Luo Hengxin described these abuses, and the rule allowing transport of tea in exchange for salt was abolished; official transport was restored under a capital official's supervision.

sentences.zh: 景泰中，罷遣行人。

translations.literal: Under Jingtai the envoys were withdrawn.
translations.idiomatic: Under Jingtai the envoys were withdrawn.

sentences.zh: 成化三年命御史巡茶陝西。

translations.literal: In the third year of Chenghua censors were ordered to inspect tea in Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Chenghua censors were ordered to inspect tea in Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 番人不樂御史，馬至日少。

translations.literal: The tribes resented the censors, and fewer horses arrived each day.
translations.idiomatic: The tribes resented the censors, and fewer horses arrived each day.

sentences.zh: 乃取回御史，仍遣行人，且令按察司巡察。

translations.literal: The censors were recalled, envoys were sent out again, and the Surveillance Commission was also ordered to inspect.
translations.idiomatic: The censors were recalled, envoys were sent out again, and the Surveillance Commission was also ordered to inspect.

sentences.zh: 已而巡察不專，兵部言其害，乃復遣御史，歲一更，著為令。

translations.literal: When inspection became unfocused, the Ministry of War pointed out the harm, censors were sent again on annual rotation, and this was made permanent regulation.
translations.idiomatic: When inspection became unfocused, the Ministry of War pointed out the harm, censors were sent again on annual rotation, and this was made permanent regulation.

sentences.zh: 又以歲饑待振，復令商納粟中茶，且令茶百斤折銀五錢。

translations.literal: Famine relief also led to renewed merchant grain payments for tea certificates, with tea taxed at five qian of silver per hundred jin.
translations.idiomatic: Famine relief also led to renewed merchant grain payments for tea certificates, with tea taxed at five qian of silver per hundred jin.

sentences.zh: 商課折色自此始。

translations.literal: From this date merchant taxes could be paid in silver instead of goods.
translations.idiomatic: From this date merchant taxes could be paid in silver instead of goods.

sentences.zh: 弘治三年，御史李鸞言：「茶馬司所積漸少，各邊馬耗，而陝西諸郡歲稔，無事易粟。

translations.literal: In the third year of Hongzhi, Censor Li Luan said: "Stores at the Tea and Horse Offices are dwindling, frontier horses are scarce, yet Shaanxi's prefectures enjoy good harvests and have no need to trade grain.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Hongzhi, Censor Li Luan reported: "Stores at the Tea and Horse Offices are dwindling, frontier horses are scarce, yet Shaanxi's prefectures enjoy good harvests and have no need to trade grain.

sentences.zh: 請於西寧、河西、洮州三茶馬司召商中茶，每引不過百斤，每商不過三十引，官收其十之四，餘者始令貨賣，可得茶四十萬斤，易馬四千匹，數足而止。」

translations.literal: He asked that merchants be summoned to the three offices at Xining, Hexi, and Taozhou to buy certificates — no more than one hundred jin per permit or thirty permits per merchant — with the state taking four-tenths and the remainder sold privately, yielding 400,000 jin of tea to buy four thousand horses, stopping when the quota was met."
translations.idiomatic: He asked that merchants be summoned to the three offices at Xining, Hexi, and Taozhou to buy certificates — no more than one hundred jin per permit or thirty permits per merchant — with the state taking four-tenths and the remainder sold privately, yielding 400,000 jin of tea to buy four thousand horses, stopping when the quota was met.

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: The emperor approved it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved the proposal.

sentences.zh: 十二年，御史王憲又言：「自中茶禁開，遂令私茶莫遏，而易馬不利。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year, Censor Wang Xian again said: "Since the tea-certificate ban was relaxed, private tea has become unstoppable and horse trade has suffered.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year, Censor Wang Xian again reported: "Since the tea-certificate ban was relaxed, private tea has become unstoppable and the horse trade has suffered.

sentences.zh: 請停糧茶之例。

translations.literal: He requested that the grain-for-tea regulation be suspended.
translations.idiomatic: He requested that the grain-for-tea regulation be suspended.

sentences.zh: 異時或兵荒，乃更圖之。」

translations.literal: If war or famine should arise later, the matter can be reconsidered then."
translations.idiomatic: If war or famine should arise later, the matter can be reconsidered then.

sentences.zh: 部覆從其請。

translations.literal: The ministry replied and approved his request.
translations.idiomatic: The ministry replied and approved his request.

sentences.zh: 四川茶課司舊徵數十萬斤易馬。

translations.literal: The Sichuan Tea Tax Office had formerly levied several hundred thousand jin for horse trade.
translations.idiomatic: The Sichuan Tea Tax Office had formerly levied several hundred thousand jin for horse trade.

sentences.zh: 永樂以後，番馬悉由陝西道，川茶多浥爛。

translations.literal: After Yongle, tribal horses all came via the Shaanxi route, and much Sichuan tea soaked and rotted.
translations.idiomatic: After Yongle, tribal horses all came via the Shaanxi route, and much Sichuan tea soaked and rotted.

sentences.zh: 乃令以三分為率，一分收本色，二分折銀，糧茶停二年。

translations.literal: It was then ordered that of every three parts, one be collected in kind and two converted to silver; the grain-for-tea system was suspended for two years.
translations.idiomatic: It was then ordered that of every three parts, one be collected in kind and two converted to silver; the grain-for-tea system was suspended for two years.

sentences.zh: 延綏饑，復召商納糧草，中四百萬斤。

translations.literal: When Yanbian suffered famine, merchants were again summoned to pay grain and fodder for certificates totaling four million jin.
translations.idiomatic: When Yanbian suffered famine, merchants were again summoned to pay grain and fodder for certificates totaling four million jin.

sentences.zh: 尋以御史王紹言，復禁止，並罷正額外召商開中之例。

translations.literal: Soon, on Censor Wang Shao's recommendation, the practice was again prohibited, and the rule of summoning merchants beyond the regular quota for open certificates was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Soon, on Censor Wang Shao's recommendation, the practice was again prohibited, and the rule of summoning merchants beyond the regular quota for open certificates was abolished.

sentences.zh: 十六年取回御史，以督理馬政都御史楊一清兼理之。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year the censor was recalled, and Censor-in-Chief Yang Yiqing, overseer of horse administration, was given concurrent charge of tea affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year the censor was recalled, and Censor-in-Chief Yang Yiqing, overseer of horse administration, was given concurrent charge of tea affairs.

sentences.zh: 一清復議開中，言：「召商買茶，官貿其三之一，每歲茶五六十萬斤，可得馬萬匹。」

translations.literal: Yiqing again proposed reviving open certificates, saying: "Summon merchants to buy tea; the government shall purchase one-third. Each year five or six hundred thousand jin of tea could bring ten thousand horses."
translations.idiomatic: Yiqing again proposed reviving open certificates, saying: "Summon merchants to buy tea; the government shall purchase one-third. Each year five or six hundred thousand jin of tea could bring ten thousand horses.

sentences.zh: 帝從所請。

translations.literal: The emperor approved the request.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved the request.

sentences.zh: 正德元年，一清又建議，商人不願領價者，以半與商，令自賣。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhengde, Yiqing proposed again that merchants unwilling to receive payment in cash be given half the tea to sell themselves.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Zhengde, Yiqing proposed again that merchants unwilling to receive payment in cash be given half the tea to sell themselves.

sentences.zh: 遂著為例永行焉。

translations.literal: This was then fixed as a permanent regulation.
translations.idiomatic: This was then fixed as a permanent regulation.

sentences.zh: 一清又言金牌信符之制當復，且請復設巡茶御史兼理馬政。

translations.literal: Yiqing also said the gold-plaque credential system should be restored and requested that tea-patrol censors be reinstated with concurrent charge of horse administration.
translations.idiomatic: Yiqing also said the gold-plaque credential system should be restored and requested that tea-patrol censors be reinstated with concurrent charge of horse administration.

sentences.zh: 乃復遣御史，而金牌以久廢。

translations.literal: Censors were again dispatched, but the gold plaques had long been abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: Censors were again dispatched, but the gold plaques had long been abandoned.

sentences.zh: 卒不能復。

translations.literal: In the end they could not be restored.
translations.idiomatic: In the end they could not be restored.

sentences.zh: 後武宗寵番僧，許西域人例外帶私茶。

translations.literal: Later, when Wuzong favored tribal monks, Western Regions people were permitted to carry private tea as an exception.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when Wuzong favored tribal monks, Western Regions people were permitted to carry private tea as an exception.

sentences.zh: 自是茶法遂壞。

translations.literal: From this the tea law collapsed.
translations.idiomatic: From this the tea law collapsed.

sentences.zh: 番人之市馬也，不能辯權衡，止訂篦中馬。

translations.literal: When tribes traded horses they could not use standard weights and measures, and fixed only the number of bamboo tea baskets per horse.
translations.idiomatic: When tribes traded horses they could not use standard weights and measures, and fixed only the number of bamboo tea baskets per horse.

sentences.zh: 篦大，則官虧其直；

translations.literal: If the baskets were large, the government lost on the exchange;
translations.idiomatic: If the baskets were large, the government lost on the exchange;

sentences.zh: 小，則商病其繁。

translations.literal: if they were small, merchants suffered from the burden.
translations.idiomatic: if they were small, merchants suffered from the burden.

sentences.zh: 十年巡茶御史王汝舟酌為中制，每千斤為三百三十篦。

translations.literal: In the tenth year Tea Patrol Censor Wang Ruzhou set a middle standard of three hundred thirty baskets per thousand jin.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year Tea Patrol Censor Wang Ruzhou set a middle standard of three hundred thirty baskets per thousand jin.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖三年，御史陳講以商茶低偽，悉徵黑茶，地產有限，乃第茶為上中二品，印烙篦上，書商名而考之。

translations.literal: In the third year of Jiajing, Censor Chen Jiang, because merchant tea was inferior and spurious, levied only black tea; as local production was limited, tea was ranked in upper and middle grades, stamped on the baskets, with merchant names written for inspection.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Jiajing, Censor Chen Jiang, because merchant tea was inferior and spurious, levied only black tea; as local production was limited, tea was ranked in upper and middle grades, stamped on the baskets, with merchant names written for inspection.

sentences.zh: 旋定四川茶引五萬道，二萬六千道為腹引，二萬四千道為邊引。

translations.literal: Sichuan tea permits were soon fixed at fifty thousand certificates: twenty-six thousand as interior permits and twenty-four thousand as border permits.
translations.idiomatic: Sichuan tea permits were soon fixed at fifty thousand certificates: twenty-six thousand as interior permits and twenty-four thousand as border permits.

sentences.zh: 芽茶引三錢，葉茶引二錢。

translations.literal: Bud-tea permits cost three qian; leaf-tea permits cost two qian.
translations.idiomatic: Bud-tea permits cost three qian; leaf-tea permits cost two qian.

sentences.zh: 中茶至八十萬斤而止，不得太濫。

translations.literal: Tea certificates were capped at eight hundred thousand jin and were not to be issued too freely.
translations.idiomatic: Tea certificates were capped at eight hundred thousand jin and were not to be issued too freely.

sentences.zh: 十五年，御史劉良卿言：「律例：『私茶出境與關隘失察者，並淩遲處死。』

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year, Censor Liu Liangqing said: "The statute reads: 'Those who smuggle private tea across the border and pass officials who fail to detect it shall both be executed by lingering death.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year, Censor Liu Liangqing said: "The statute reads: 'Those who smuggle private tea across the border and pass officials who fail to detect it shall both be executed by lingering death.

sentences.zh: 蓋西陲籓籬，莫切於諸番。

translations.literal: For the western frontier barrier, nothing is more urgent than the frontier tribes.
