translations.idiomatic: For the western frontier barrier, nothing is more urgent than the frontier tribes.

sentences.zh: 番人恃茶以生，故嚴法以禁之，易馬以酬之，以制番人之死命，壯中國之籓籬，斷匈奴之右臂，非可以常法論也。

translations.literal: The tribes rely on tea to live; therefore strict laws prohibit it, horses are exchanged to reward them, to control the tribes' very livelihood, strengthen China's frontier barrier, and sever the Xiongnu's right arm — this cannot be judged by ordinary law.
translations.idiomatic: The tribes rely on tea to live; therefore strict laws prohibit it and horses are exchanged to reward them, to control the tribes' very livelihood, strengthen China's frontier barrier, and sever the Xiongnu's right arm — this cannot be judged by ordinary law.

sentences.zh: 洪武初例，民間蓄茶不得過一月之用。

translations.literal: An early Hongwu regulation held that private tea storage must not exceed one month's supply.
translations.idiomatic: An early Hongwu regulation held that private tea storage must not exceed one month's supply.

sentences.zh: 弘治中，召商中茶，或以備振，或以儲邊，然未嘗禁內地之民使不得食茶也。

translations.literal: Under Hongzhi, merchants were summoned to buy tea certificates, sometimes for famine relief or frontier stores, yet the people of the interior were never forbidden to drink tea.
translations.idiomatic: Under Hongzhi, merchants were summoned to buy tea certificates, sometimes for famine relief or frontier stores, yet the people of the interior were never forbidden to drink tea.

sentences.zh: 今減通番之罪，止於充軍。

translations.literal: Now the offense of trading with the tribes has been reduced to military exile alone.
translations.idiomatic: Now the offense of trading with the tribes has been reduced to military exile alone.

sentences.zh: 禁內地之茶，使不得食，又使商私課茶，悉聚於三茶馬司。

translations.literal: Tea in the interior is prohibited so people cannot consume it, and merchants' private duty tea is all gathered at the three Tea and Horse Offices.
translations.idiomatic: Tea in the interior is prohibited so people cannot consume it, and merchants' private duty tea is all gathered at the three Tea and Horse Offices.

sentences.zh: 夫茶司與番為鄰，私販易通，而禁復嚴於內郡，是驅民為私販而授之資也。

translations.literal: The tea offices border the tribes, so private trade passes easily, yet the ban is stricter than in interior commanderies — this drives the people into smuggling and hands them the means.
translations.idiomatic: The tea offices border the tribes, so private trade passes easily, yet the ban is stricter than in interior commanderies — this drives the people into smuggling and hands them the means.

sentences.zh: 以故大奸闌出而漏網，小民負升鬥而罹法。

translations.literal: Thus great villains slip through and escape the net, while common people carrying sheng and dou of tea fall under the law.
translations.idiomatic: Thus great villains slip through and escape the net, while common people carrying sheng and dou of tea fall under the law.

sentences.zh: 今計三茶馬司所貯，洮河足三年，西寧足二年，而商、私、課茶又日益增，積久腐爛而無所用。

translations.literal: Counting stores at the three Tea and Horse Offices today: Tao-He has enough for three years, Xining for two, yet merchant, private, and duty tea keep increasing daily, piling up until they rot with no use.
translations.idiomatic: Counting stores at the three Tea and Horse Offices today: Tao-He has enough for three years, Xining for two, yet merchant, private, and duty tea keep increasing daily, piling up until they rot with no use.

sentences.zh: 茶法之弊如此。

translations.literal: Such are the abuses of the tea law.
translations.idiomatic: Such are the abuses of the tea law.

sentences.zh: 番地多馬而無所市，吾茶有禁而不得通，其勢必相求，而制之之機在我。

translations.literal: The tribal lands have many horses but nowhere to sell them; our tea is under prohibition and cannot circulate — the situation must lead them to seek each other, and the leverage to control it lies with us.
translations.idiomatic: The tribes have horses in abundance but no market for them, while our tea is barred from trade — inevitably the two sides will seek each other out, and the power to regulate that exchange rests in our hands.

sentences.zh: 今茶司居民，竊易番馬以待商販，歲無虛日，及官易時，而馬反耗矣。

translations.literal: Now the people living at the tea offices secretly trade for tribal horses to await merchant sales; not a day in the year goes unused, yet when official exchange comes, horses have in fact been depleted.
translations.idiomatic: Today the residents around the tea offices quietly buy tribal horses in advance for private resale, keeping busy year-round — so that by the time the official exchange season arrives, the supply of horses has already been drained.

sentences.zh: 請敕三茶馬司，止留二年之用，每年易馬當發若干。

translations.literal: It is requested that an imperial order be sent to the three Tea and Horse Offices to keep only two years' supply and to set how many horses should be issued for exchange each year.
translations.idiomatic: He asked that the three Tea and Horse Offices be ordered to hold no more than a two-year reserve and to fix the number of horses traded each year.

sentences.zh: 正茶之外，分毫毋得夾帶。

translations.literal: Beyond official quota tea, not a fraction may be smuggled in.
translations.idiomatic: Nothing beyond the official quota tea may be included — not even the smallest amount.

sentences.zh: 令茶價踴貴，番人受制，良馬將不可勝用。

translations.literal: Cause tea prices to soar; the tribes will be constrained, and fine horses will soon be more than can be used.
translations.idiomatic: Let tea prices rise steeply so the tribes depend on us, and good horses will flow in beyond what we can use.

sentences.zh: 且多開商茶，通行內地，官榷其半以備軍餉，而河、蘭、階、岷諸近番地，禁賣如故，更重通番之刑如律例。

translations.literal: Moreover, broadly open merchant tea, let it circulate in the interior, let the government monopolize half to prepare military provisions, while He, Lan, Jie, Min and other places near the tribes remain under sale prohibitions as before, and increase penalties for trading with the tribes according to the statutes.
translations.idiomatic: At the same time, open up merchant tea for sale throughout the interior, with the government levying half the proceeds for military supplies, while places near the tribes — He, Lan, Jie, and Min — would remain under the old bans on tea sales and face even harsher penalties for unauthorized frontier trade.

sentences.zh: 洮、岷、河責邊備道，臨洮、蘭州責隴右分巡，西寧責兵備，各選官防守。

translations.literal: Tao, Min, and He shall be charged to the frontier defense circuit; Lintao and Lanzhou to the Longyou sub-circuit censor; Xining to the military defense commissioner — each to select officials for defense.
translations.idiomatic: Tao, Min, and He would fall under the frontier defense circuit; Lintao and Lanzhou under the Longyou sub-circuit censor; and Xining under the military defense commissioner — each charged with posting officials to guard against smuggling.

sentences.zh: 失察者以罷軟論。」

translations.literal: Those who fail in oversight shall be judged by the standard for laxity."
translations.idiomatic: Officials who failed to detect violations would be dismissed for incompetence.

sentences.zh: 奏上，報可。

translations.literal: The memorial was submitted, and approval was returned.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was submitted and approved.

sentences.zh: 於是茶法稍飭矣。

translations.literal: Thus the tea law was somewhat rectified.
translations.idiomatic: The tea regulations were partly restored to order.

sentences.zh: 御史劉侖、總督尚書王以旂等，請復給諸番金牌信符。

translations.literal: Censor Liu Lun, Grand Coordinator Minister Wang Yiqi, and others requested that gold-plaque credentials be restored and given again to the various tribes.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Liu Lun, Grand Coordinator Wang Yiqi, and others asked that the gold-plaque credentials be issued again to the frontier tribes.

sentences.zh: 兵部議，番族變詐不常，北狄抄掠無已，金牌亟給亟失，殊損國體。

translations.literal: The Ministry of War deliberated: tribal peoples are fickle and deceitful; northern barbarians raid without end; gold plaques are given and lost in rapid succession — this greatly damages state dignity.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of War argued that the tribes were treacherous and unpredictable, that northern raiders never stopped, and that gold plaques were lost as fast as they were issued — all of which shamed the state.

sentences.zh: 番人納馬，意在得茶，嚴私販之禁，則番人自順，雖不給金牌，馬可集也。

translations.literal: Tribes who submit horses intend to obtain tea; if the private-trade ban is strictly enforced, the tribes will naturally comply — even without giving gold plaques, horses can be gathered.
translations.idiomatic: The tribes brought horses because they wanted tea; tighten the ban on smuggling and they would come willingly — horses could be collected even without restoring the gold plaques.

sentences.zh: 若私販盛行，吾無以系其心、制其命，雖給金牌，馬亦不至。

translations.literal: If private trade flourishes, we have no means to bind their hearts and control their livelihoods; even if gold plaques are given, horses will not arrive.
translations.idiomatic: But if smuggling flourished, we would lose all leverage over them; even with gold plaques, no horses would come.

sentences.zh: 乃定議發勘合予之。

translations.literal: They therefore fixed the decision to issue verification tallies and grant them.
translations.idiomatic: In the end they agreed to issue verification tallies instead.

sentences.zh: 其後陝西歲饑，茶戶無所資，頗逋課額。

translations.literal: Afterward Shaanxi suffered famine year by year; tea households had no means of support and considerably defaulted on their tax quotas.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when famine struck Shaanxi, tea growers had no livelihood and fell far behind on their tax payments.

sentences.zh: 三十六年，戶部以全陝災震，邊餉告急，國用大絀，上言：「先時，正額茶易馬之外，多開中以佐公家，有至五百萬斤者。

translations.literal: In the thirty-sixth year, the Ministry of Revenue, because all Shaanxi suffered disaster and earthquake, frontier provisions were urgently reported short, and state expenditure was greatly strained, memorialized: "Formerly, beyond regular-quota tea for horse exchange, open certificates were additionally opened to assist the public treasury, reaching as much as five million jin.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-sixth year the Ministry of Revenue reported that earthquakes and disaster had ravaged Shaanxi, frontier supplies were critically low, and the treasury was severely overextended: "In earlier times, besides the regular tea quota traded for horses, additional certificate openings had supplemented government revenues — in some years reaching five million jin.

sentences.zh: 近者御史劉良卿亦開百萬，後止開正額八十萬斤，並課茶、私茶通計僅九十餘萬。

translations.literal: Recently Censor Liu Liangqing also opened one million; afterward only the regular quota of eight hundred thousand jin was opened, and counting duty tea and private tea together amounted to barely nine hundred thousand-plus.
translations.idiomatic: Recently Censor Liu Liangqing had opened certificates for another million jin, but the quota had since been cut to eight hundred thousand jin of regular tea, with duty and private tea bringing the total to barely nine hundred thousand jin.

sentences.zh: 宜下巡茶御史議，召商多中。」

translations.literal: It is fitting to send this down to the tea-patrol censor for deliberation and summon merchants to bid for more certificates."
translations.idiomatic: The ministry urged sending the matter to the tea-patrol censor and summoning merchants to tender for additional certificates.

sentences.zh: 御史楊美益言：「歲祲民貧，即正額尚多虧損，安有贏羨。

translations.literal: Censor Yang Meiyi said: "In years of famine the people are poor; even the regular quota still shows heavy losses — how could there be surplus?
translations.idiomatic: Censor Yang Meiyi replied: "In a famine year the people are destitute — even the regular quota falls short. Where is there any surplus?

sentences.zh: 今第宜守每年九十萬斤招番易馬之規。

translations.literal: Now it is only fitting to uphold the rule of nine hundred thousand jin each year to summon tribes and exchange for horses.
translations.idiomatic: For now we should simply adhere to the rule of nine hundred thousand jin per year for trading with the tribes.

sentences.zh: 凡通內地以息私販，增開中以備振荒，悉從停罷，毋使與馬分利。」

translations.literal: All measures to open the interior to stop private trade, and to increase open certificates to prepare famine relief, should entirely be halted, so that they do not share profit with the horse trade."
translations.idiomatic: Proposals to open interior trade to curb smuggling and to increase certificate openings for famine relief should all be dropped, so that tea revenue is not diverted from the horse trade.

sentences.zh: 戶部以帑藏方匱，請如弘治六年例，易馬外仍開百萬斤，召納邊鎮以備軍餉。

translations.literal: The Ministry of Revenue, because the treasury was just then depleted, requested that according to the sixth year of Hongzhi precedent, beyond horse exchange one million jin still be opened, summoning payment to frontier garrisons to prepare military provisions.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of Revenue, citing the depleted treasury, asked that — following the Hongzhi sixth-year precedent — an additional million jin of certificates be opened beyond the horse-trade quota, with proceeds sent to frontier garrisons for military pay.

sentences.zh: 詔從之。

translations.literal: An edict followed the request.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 末年，御史潘一桂言：「增中商茶頗壅滯，宜裁減十四五。」

translations.literal: In the final years, Censor Pan Yigui said: "The increased merchant tea certificates are quite congested and stagnant; it is fitting to cut them by fourteen or fifteen percent."
translations.idiomatic: Near the end of the reign, Censor Pan Yigui reported that the expanded merchant tea certificates were backing up badly and should be cut by fourteen or fifteen percent.

sentences.zh: 又言：「松潘與洮、河近，私茶往往闌出，宜停松潘引目，申嚴入番之禁。」

translations.literal: He also said: "Songpan is near Tao and He; private tea often slips through — it is fitting to halt Songpan certificate quotas and strictly reenforce the ban on entering tribal lands."
translations.idiomatic: He also argued that because Songpan lay close to Tao and He, smuggled tea often leaked through there — Songpan's certificate quota should be suspended and the ban on tea entering tribal territory tightened.

sentences.zh: 皆報可。

translations.literal: All were approved.
translations.idiomatic: Both proposals were approved.

sentences.zh: 四川茶引之分邊腹也，邊茶少而易行，腹茶多而常滯。

translations.literal: Sichuan tea certificates were divided into frontier and interior: frontier tea was little and moved easily; interior tea was much and often stagnant.
translations.idiomatic: In Sichuan, tea certificates were split between frontier and interior regions — frontier allotments were small and sold readily, while interior allotments were large and often went unsold.

sentences.zh: 隆慶三年裁引萬二千，以三萬引屬黎、雅，四千引屬松潘諸邊，四千引留內地，稅銀共萬四千餘兩，解部濟邊以為常。

translations.literal: In the third year of Longqing, twelve thousand certificates were cut; thirty thousand certificates were assigned to Li and Ya, four thousand to Songpan and other frontier areas, four thousand kept in the interior, tax silver totaling more than fourteen thousand taels, remitted to the ministry to aid the frontier as a fixed rule.
translations.idiomatic: In Longqing 3 the quota was cut by twelve thousand certificates: thirty thousand went to Li and Ya prefectures, four thousand to Songpan and other frontier posts, and four thousand to the interior — yielding over fourteen thousand taels of tax silver remitted annually to the ministry for frontier aid.

sentences.zh: 五年令甘州仿洮、河、西寧事例，歲以六月開中，兩月內中馬八百匹。

translations.literal: In the fifth year Ganzhou was ordered to follow the Tao, He, and Xining precedent: each year in the sixth month open certificates, within two months tender for eight hundred horses.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year Ganzhou was ordered to adopt the same system as Tao, He, and Xining — opening certificates each June and completing tenders for eight hundred horses within two months.

sentences.zh: 立賞罰例，商引一二年銷完者賞有差，逾三年者罪之，沒其附帶茶。

translations.literal: Reward and penalty regulations were established: merchants whose certificates were sold out within one or two years received graded rewards; those exceeding three years were punished and their accompanying tea confiscated.
translations.idiomatic: Rewards and penalties were set: merchants who cleared their certificates within one or two years received graded rewards; those who took more than three years were penalized and any extra tea they carried was confiscated.

sentences.zh: 萬曆五年，俺答款塞，請開茶市。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Wanli, Altan submitted at the frontier and requested opening a tea market.
translations.idiomatic: In Wanli 5 Altan Khan submitted to the dynasty and asked for a tea market to be opened.

sentences.zh: 御史李時成言：「番以茶為命，北狄若得，藉以制番，番必從狄，貽患匪細。

translations.literal: Censor Li Shicheng said: "The tribes take tea as their livelihood; if the northern barbarians obtain it, they will use it to control the tribes — the tribes must follow the Di, and the harm would not be slight.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Li Shicheng warned: "Tea is life itself for the tribes. If the northern steppe peoples gained access to it, they could use tea to dominate the tribes, who would then align with the northerners — the consequences would be grave.

sentences.zh: 部議給百餘篦，而勿許其市易。

translations.literal: The ministry deliberated to give more than one hundred bamboo baskets but not permit market exchange.
translations.idiomatic: The ministry agreed to grant a little over a hundred baskets of tea as tribute but refused to allow open trading.

sentences.zh: 自劉良卿馳內地之禁，楊美益以為非，其後復禁止。

translations.literal: From when Liu Liangqing hurried the interior ban, Yang Meiyi considered it wrong, and afterward it was again prohibited.
translations.idiomatic: After Liu Liangqing had rushed to ban interior tea sales, Yang Meiyi objected — and the ban was eventually reimposed.

sentences.zh: 十三年，以西安、鳳翔、漢中不與番鄰，開其禁，招商給引，抽十三入官，餘聽自賣。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year, because Xi'an, Fengxiang, and Hanzhong do not border the tribes, their bans were opened; merchants were summoned and certificates given, thirteen parts taken for the government, the remainder permitted to sell freely.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year, because Xi'an, Fengxiang, and Hanzhong did not border tribal territory, the bans there were lifted — merchants were recruited, certificates issued, with one part in thirteen taken for the government and the rest free to sell.

sentences.zh: 御史鐘化民以私茶之闌出多也，請分任責成。

translations.literal: Censor Zhong Huamin, because private tea frequently slipped through illegally, requested dividing responsibility and fixing accountability.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Zhong Huamin, noting how much smuggled tea was getting through, asked that enforcement duties be divided and officials held accountable.

sentences.zh: 陝之漢中，關南道督之，府佐一人專駐魚渡壩；

translations.literal: Hanzhong in Shaanxi — the Guannan circuit would supervise it, one assistant prefect permanently stationed at Yuduba Dam;
translations.idiomatic: In Shaanxi's Hanzhong, the Guannan circuit would oversee enforcement, with one assistant prefect permanently posted at Yuduba Pass;

sentences.zh: 川之保寧，川北道督之，府佐一人專駐雞猴壩。

translations.literal: Baoning in Sichuan — the Chuanbei circuit would supervise it, one assistant prefect permanently stationed at Jihouba Dam.
translations.idiomatic: In Sichuan's Baoning, the Chuanbei circuit would take charge, with one assistant prefect stationed at Jihouba Pass.

sentences.zh: 率州、縣官兵防守。」

translations.literal: Leading prefecture and county troops and officials in defense."
translations.idiomatic: They would command local troops and officials to guard the passes.

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: Approval followed.
translations.idiomatic: The proposal was approved.

sentences.zh: 中茶易馬，惟漢中、保寧，而湖南產茶，其直賤，商人率越境私販，中漢中、保寧者，僅一二十引。

translations.literal: Tending tea certificates for horse exchange was only at Hanzhong and Baoning, yet Hunan produces tea and its price is cheap; merchants generally crossed borders in private trade, and those who tendered at Hanzhong and Baoning numbered barely ten or twenty certificates.
translations.idiomatic: Certificate tenders for tea-and-horse exchange were accepted only at Hanzhong and Baoning, but Hunan produced cheap tea and merchants routinely smuggled it across the border — so only ten or twenty certificates a year were tendered at Hanzhong and Baoning.

sentences.zh: 茶戶欲辦本課，輒私販出邊，番族利私茶之賤，因不肯納馬。

translations.literal: Tea households wishing to meet their basic tax quota frequently smuggled tea beyond the frontier; tribal peoples profited from cheap private tea and therefore refused to submit horses.
translations.idiomatic: Tea growers trying to meet their tax obligations smuggled tea to the frontier, where tribes favored the cheap contraband and stopped offering horses to the official markets.

sentences.zh: 二十三年，御史李楠請禁湖茶，言：「湖茶行，茶法、馬政兩弊，宜令巡茶御史召商給引，願報漢、興、保、夔者，準中。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year, Censor Li Nan requested banning Hunan tea, saying: "When Hunan tea circulates, both tea law and horse administration are harmed — it is fitting to order the tea-patrol censor to summon merchants and issue certificates; those willing to register at Han, Xing, Bao, and Kui should be permitted to tender.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-third year Censor Li Nan asked to ban Hunan tea, arguing that its spread was ruining both the tea monopoly and horse policy: the tea-patrol censor should summon merchants and issue certificates to those willing to trade through Hanzhong, Xing'an, Baoning, and Kuizhou.

sentences.zh: 越境下湖南者，禁止。

translations.literal: Those crossing borders downstream to Hunan — prohibit.
translations.idiomatic: Anyone who crossed the border to sell in Hunan should be barred.

sentences.zh: 且湖南多假茶，食之刺口破腹，番人亦受其害。」

translations.literal: Moreover Hunan has much counterfeit tea; eating it stings the mouth and ruptures the belly — tribal peoples also suffer harm from it."
translations.idiomatic: Hunan also produced much adulterated tea that burned the mouth and upset the stomach — harming the tribes as well.

sentences.zh: 既而御史徐僑言：「漢、川茶少而直高，湖南茶多而直下。

translations.literal: Then Censor Xu Qiao said: "Han and Sichuan tea is little and its price high; Hunan tea is abundant and its price low.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Xu Qiao countered: "Hanzhong and Sichuan teas are scarce and costly, while Hunan tea is abundant and cheap.

sentences.zh: 湖茶之行，無妨漢中。

translations.literal: The circulation of Hunan tea does not obstruct Hanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: Hunan tea posed no threat to Hanzhong's market.

sentences.zh: 漢茶味甘而薄，湖茶味苦，於酥酪為宜，亦利番也。

translations.literal: Han tea's taste is sweet and light; Hunan tea's flavor is bitter — for butter-tea it is suitable, and it also benefits the tribes.
translations.idiomatic: Han tea was sweet and mild, Hunan tea bitter — better suited to buttered tea and beneficial to the tribes as well.

sentences.zh: 但宜立法嚴核，以遏假茶。」

translations.literal: Only it is fitting to establish laws for strict inspection to check counterfeit tea."
translations.idiomatic: But strict inspection laws were needed to stop adulterated tea.

sentences.zh: 戶部折衷其議，以漢茶為主，湖茶佐之。

translations.literal: The Ministry of Revenue split the difference in their proposals, taking Han tea as primary and Hunan tea as auxiliary.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of Revenue split the difference, making Hanzhong tea primary and Hunan tea supplementary.

sentences.zh: 各商中引，先給漢、川畢，乃給湖南。

translations.literal: For each merchant's certificate tender, Han and Sichuan are fully issued first, then Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: Merchants tendering for certificates would receive Hanzhong and Sichuan allotments first; Hunan allotments came only after those were filled.

sentences.zh: 如漢引不足，則補以湖引。

translations.literal: If Han certificates are insufficient, then supplement with Hunan certificates.
translations.idiomatic: If Hanzhong certificates ran short, Hunan certificates would make up the difference.

sentences.zh: 報可。

translations.literal: Approval was returned.
translations.idiomatic: The compromise was approved.

sentences.zh: 二十九年，陝西巡按御史畢三才言：「課茶徵輸，歲有定額。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year, Shaanxi touring censor Bi Sancai said: "Duty tea collection and delivery has a fixed quota each year.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-ninth year Shaanxi touring censor Bi Sancai reported that duty tea payments were fixed at an annual quota.

sentences.zh: 先因茶多餘積，園戶解納艱難，以此改折。

translations.literal: Formerly because tea accumulated in surplus and garden households found delivery in kind difficult, for this reason commutation to cash was adopted.
translations.idiomatic: Because surplus tea had piled up and growers struggled to deliver their quotas in kind, the levy had been converted to cash payments.

sentences.zh: 今商人絕跡，五司茶空。

translations.literal: Now merchants have entirely vanished; the five offices' tea is empty.
translations.idiomatic: Now no merchants came at all, and the tea stores at the five offices stood empty.

sentences.zh: 請令漢中五州縣仍輸本色，每歲招商中五百引，可得馬萬一千九百餘匹。」

translations.literal: It is requested to order the five prefectures and counties of Hanzhong still to deliver payment in kind; each year summon merchants to tender five hundred certificates, which can obtain more than eleven thousand nine hundred horses."
translations.idiomatic: He asked that the five Hanzhong prefectures and counties resume delivery in kind, and that five hundred certificates be opened each year — enough to bring in over eleven thousand nine hundred horses.

sentences.zh: 部議，西寧、河、洮、岷、甘、莊浪六茶司共易馬九千六百匹，著為令。

translations.literal: The ministry deliberated: the six tea offices of Xining, He, Tao, Min, Gan, and Zhuanglang together exchange for nine thousand six hundred horses, fixed as a regulation.
translations.idiomatic: The ministry settled on nine thousand six hundred horses per year across the six tea offices at Xining, He, Tao, Min, Gan, and Zhuanglang, and made that the standing quota.

sentences.zh: 天啟時，增中馬二千四百匹。

translations.literal: At the time of Tianqi, certificate tenders for horses were increased by two thousand four hundred.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tianqi reign the horse quota was raised by another twenty-four hundred.

sentences.zh: 明初嚴禁私販，久而奸弊日生。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Ming, private trade was strictly prohibited; over time deceitful abuses arose day by day.
translations.idiomatic: The dynasty had strictly banned smuggling at the outset, but abuses multiplied over the years.

sentences.zh: 洎乎末造，商人正引之外，多給賞由票，使得私行。

translations.literal: By the final years, beyond merchants' regular certificates, many reward transfer tickets were additionally given, allowing them to travel privately.
translations.idiomatic: By the dynasty's final years, merchants received extra reward passes beyond their regular certificates, allowing them to trade tea privately.

sentences.zh: 番人上駟盡入奸商，茶司所市者乃其中下也。

translations.literal: The tribes' finest horses all entered corrupt merchants; what the tea offices purchased were only their middling and lower grades.
translations.idiomatic: The finest tribal horses all went to corrupt private traders, leaving only mediocre stock for the official tea offices.

sentences.zh: 番得茶，叛服自由；

translations.literal: Tribes obtaining tea — submission and rebellion at their own will;
translations.idiomatic: Once the tribes had tea, they submitted or rebelled as they pleased;

sentences.zh: 而將吏又以私馬竄番馬，冒支上茶。

translations.literal: While generals and officials also substituted private horses for tribal horses, fraudulently drawing premium tea.
translations.idiomatic: Officers and officials substituted their own horses for tribal horses and fraudulently claimed top-grade tea in exchange.

sentences.zh: 茶法、馬政、邊防於是俱壞矣。

translations.literal: Tea law, horse administration, and frontier defense were thus all ruined.
translations.idiomatic: The tea law, horse policy, and frontier defense all collapsed together.

sentences.zh: 其他產茶之地，南直隸常、盧、池、徽，浙江湖、嚴、衢、紹，江西南昌、饒州、南康、九江、吉安，湖廣武昌、荊州、長沙、寶慶，四川成都、重慶、嘉定、夔、瀘，商人中引則於應天、宜興、杭州三批驗所，徵茶課則於應天之江東瓜埠。

translations.literal: Other tea-producing places — Chang, Lu, Chi, and Hui in Nanzhili; Hu, Yan, Qu, and Shao in Zhejiang; Nanchang, Raozhou, Nankang, Jiujiang, and Ji'an in Jiangxi; Wuchang, Jingzhou, Changsha, and Baoqing in Huguang; Chengdu, Chongqing, Jiading, Kui, and Lu in Sichuan — when merchants tender for certificates, it is at the three inspection stations of Yingtian, Yixing, and Hangzhou; tea duties are levied at Jiangdong Guabu in Yingtian.
translations.idiomatic: Elsewhere, tea was grown in Nanzhili (Changzhou, Luzhou, Chizhou, Huizhou), Zhejiang (Huzhou, Yanzhou, Quzhou, Shaoxing), Jiangxi (Nanchang, Raozhou, Nankang, Jiujiang, Ji'an), Huguang (Wuchang, Jingzhou, Changsha, Baoqing), and Sichuan (Chengdu, Chongqing, Jiading, Kuizhou, Luzhou). Merchants tendered for certificates at inspection stations in Yingtian, Yixing, and Hangzhou, while tea duties were collected at Jiangdong Guabu in Yingtian.

sentences.zh: 自蘇、常、鎮、徽、廣德及浙江、河南、廣西、貴州皆徵鈔，雲南則徵銀。

translations.literal: From Suzhou, Changzhou, Zhenjiang, Huizhou, Guangde, and Zhejiang, Henan, Guangxi, and Guizhou — all levy paper notes; Yunnan alone levies silver.
translations.idiomatic: Suzhou, Changzhou, Zhenjiang, Huizhou, Guangde, Zhejiang, Henan, Guangxi, and Guizhou all collected duty in paper notes, while Yunnan collected silver.

sentences.zh: 其上供茶，天下貢額四千有奇，福建建甯所貢最為上品，有探春、先春、次春、紫筍及薦新等號。

translations.literal: As for tribute tea sent upward, the empire's tribute quota was a little over four thousand; what Jianning in Fujian submitted was the finest grade, with designations of Pluck-Spring, Prior-Spring, Next-Spring, Purple Bud, and New Tribute, and such names.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial tribute tea totaled a little over four thousand jin nationwide. The finest came from Jianning in Fujian, graded as Pluck-Spring, Prior-Spring, Next-Spring, Purple Bud, and Fresh Tribute, among other labels.

sentences.zh: 舊皆採而碾之，壓以銀板，為大小龍團。

translations.literal: Formerly all was picked and ground, pressed with a silver plate, made into large and small dragon cakes.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly the leaves were picked, ground, and pressed with silver plates into large and small "dragon" tea cakes.

sentences.zh: 太祖以其勞民，罷造，惟令採茶芽以進，復上供戶五百家。

translations.literal: The Taizu, because it exhausted the people, abolished manufacture, ordering only tea buds to be picked and presented; he restored five hundred tribute households.
translations.idiomatic: The founding emperor abolished cake-making as too burdensome and required only fresh tea buds as tribute, restoring five hundred dedicated tribute households.

sentences.zh: 凡貢茶，第按額以供，不具載。

translations.literal: Of all tribute tea, each is supplied according to quota; details are not fully recorded here.
translations.idiomatic: All other tribute teas were supplied according to their quotas and are not listed here in detail.
